member of the commission. mr president, after the chancellor’s comprehensive summing-up of the debate, let me just say a few words about enlargement after the european council. the commission welcomes the conclusions on enlargement of the european council, skilfully presided by the austrian presidency. these conclusions pave the way for a new consensus on enlargement in the european union. this new consensus should, above all, enhance our enlightened self-interest to extend the zone of peace, democracy and prosperity in europe, while, at the same time, ensuring our capacity to function effectively and gradually absorb new members. i want to draw your attention to three particular conclusions. firstly, the european council rightly underlines the success of eu enlargement by stating that it has proved a historic opportunity contributing to peace, security, stability, democracy and the rule of law, as well as to growth and prosperity in the union as a whole, to which chancellor schüssel rightly referred. secondly, i am satisfied that the european council did not change the criteria of accession that were agreed in copenhagen in 1993. no new criteria were set up; instead, the european council reaffirmed that it will honour its existing commitments pacta sund servanda. thus it confirmed the eu’s consolidated enlargement agenda, which covers south-eastern europe, i.e. bulgaria and romania, turkey and croatia and the other countries of the western balkans. i shall have an opportunity to talk about turkey and its reforms and commitments at this afternoon’s meeting of parliament’s committee on foreign affairs. thirdly, the european council stresses the importance of ensuring that in the future the union is able to function politically, financially and institutionally as it enlarges, and to further deepen europe’s common project. it is a very important dimension and objective for this house and for the commission. as we know, the european council will hold a debate in december 2006, and the commission was invited to report on all the relevant aspects of enlargement pertaining to the union’s absorption capacity. this corresponds by and large to parliament’s resolution following the brok report some time ago. the commission will duly and gladly present a strategy document on enlargement, including absorption capacity, as part of our enlargement package in october/november 2006. i have started to prepare that document, and we are looking forward to a substantive and responsible enlargement debate with parliament and the council. this debate should not be limited just to the eu institutions: it should also reach out to civil society, both in the member states as well as in the candidate countries. it is time to create a new consensus on eu enlargement policy, based on the consolidation of our commitments, rigorous application of conditionality and better communication with our citizens. that is the best way to ensure that enlargement remains a success story, as has now been acknowledged by the european council. ten years after the dutroux affair, belgium is again plunged into a cruel drama. two girls, stacy lemmens and nathalie mahy, have been murdered. their names are added to those of julie and mélissa, to those of an and eefje, and to that of leyla. on behalf of the european parliament, i would like to express my condolences to their families. some may think that this is a fait divers, an isolated individual incident affecting only the victims, but when does a fait divers become a matter of society? i believe that this is a matter of society and that, whether in belgium or in any other country where such tragedies may occur, we cannot remain indifferent when it is innocence itself that is killed. we have an obligation to reflect deeply on why and how in our developed and civilized societies this kind of behaviour continues to occur. that is also what politics should be for: to prevent them, to avoid them, to help the families of the victims and also to prevent the possibility that the same tragic event may be forgotten and repeated. that is why i believe that we are not yielding to the dramatic moment that public opinion is living when we stand up and remember these victims: because we are not facing a singular, isolated event, an event that merits only a place on the page of events; no, we are facing a real problem of our society that has a lot to do with the dark depth of the human soul. while i was preparing these words, news also came to me that a tragic railway accident has probably caused 40 deaths and hundreds of injuries in valencia. that is why i think it is a good occasion for us all to join in with a minute of silence to the pain of all these victims. the following is the interim report by diana wallis, on behalf of the committee of inquiry into the equitable life assurance society crisis, on the equitable life assurance society crisis [2006/2026 (ini) ] (a6-0221/2006).
mr president, mrs wallis' report is an interim report, because the committee of inquiry still has a lot of work to do. in any case, a parliamentary committee of inquiry is not a court of law, that is to say, this committee will not be able to decide whether there has been correct or incorrect behaviour on the part of the british authorities in regulating the matter; that would be for the courts of law to decide. what is being revealed at the moment are shortcomings in the european union's legislation, which is designed to allow such activities to be carried out across national borders. what we are detecting at the moment is that there is no control mechanism in cases of action across national borders. in theory - as the commission representative told us - each national authority is responsible for supervision, but when the company went bankrupt, neither the irish authorities nor the german authorities could do anything because the company's subsidiaries or branches in their respective countries were closed at the time. the 6 500 pensioners in ireland, as mentioned by mr ó neachtain, and the thousands of pensioners in germany were therefore left without any possibility of control. a parliamentary committee - i have said this before - is not a court of law, but it can draw conclusions from a legislative point of view. i think the lesson we can already draw from this is that at the moment the principle of mutual recognition, the so-called 'community passport', is not enough. when community legislation is being enacted, it must also provide for an effective control mechanism which, by eliminating the principle of the country of origin or country of provenance, effectively allows the institutions of the european union to monitor the functioning of institutions which operate across national borders. i think this is the most important conclusion we can draw at this point.

a committee of independent experts. i shall refer mainly to the phenomena of mergers and acquisitions on the european stock exchanges. over the past 30 years, technological developments, the free general and in securities markets in particular. in some european countries their share is about a third of their savings, and in others it is a fifth. the demutualisation of stock exchanges, which began in asia in the mid-1990s and was subsequently extended at the beginning of this decade to the main european stock exchanges in london, paris and frankfurt, and which is still being carried out, as is currently happening in spain with the listing process, has led to restructuring, has generated concentrations in the internal market, as is the case with euronex or the scandinavian market, and all of them are positive, insofar as they tend to reduce costs and to expand transactions and listing markets. in my view, the recent announcements of transatlantic mergers and acquisitions represent a qualitative change. however, despite the growing convergence on both sides of the atlantic, substantial differences between the two markets persist, which have been identified both in the stock market model and in the market structure itself or in the elements of post-trade. it also comes at a time when the european union, having adopted the mfi directive and when it comes to its future application, is aiming to complete the european financial market. at the same time, a major debate has been initiated on the updating of the stock markets. a debate on its role in the future, on organisation, structures, transparency, economic aspects, competition, governance and infrastructure. we are at a time of very important changes. there are therefore many questions to be answered and it is therefore not a question of simply acting on a case-by-case basis, but of formulating the general interests of the european union, assessing the impact of the operations announced on them, anticipating the consequences of the operations from the political, regulatory and economic point of view and, of course, seeking the best response, knowing that financial and stock market policy has important effects on the monetary policy of the european union. and i think it is also necessary to assess the best way of ensuring transparency, stability and balance on the part of the european union for the proper functioning of the financial markets as a whole. this is the task we must carry out.

as the first item on our agenda, i shall make a statement on the 70th anniversary of the coup d'état of general franco in spain on 18 july 1936. as you know, a group of 200 members signed an oral question to the commission and the council, the purpose of which was explicitly stated as being to discuss condemnation of the franco regime on the 70th anniversary of the francoist coup d'état. the conference of presidents did not accept this request and considered it more appropriate to have a statement by the president, followed by the various political groups' views on the significance of this date; that is what we are doing now. it is a date already far in history: 70 years separate us from july 18, 1936. it is almost as much as the life expectancy of the generation of spaniards that we are leading the transition to democracy, a transition considered model, but whose success needed selective forgetting or postponements of memory, which now emerges in a recovery process that fills the bookstores and is even shaped into laws. as i said two years ago, i belong to this generation - as do many of the spanish members of parliament here - and it is inevitable that my personal relationship with the past will determine my memory. but this is an institutional statement, as speaker of the house, and my remembrance today must be a political act that transcends the personal. because bringing our past into the present is an act of will that has to do, above all, with the future we want to build, and we want to build it not only on the fragile and perishable memory of each one, but on history, which is not remembered, but learned, and which, for that reason, can be shared. and history tells us that on that day part of the spanish army - only part - rose up against the government of the second republic, democratically elected by the spanish in 1931. a great hope was thus frustrated, because this republic had come with the spirit of promoting democracy and tackling pending reforms of great depth: the agrarian, the military, the separation of church and state, the establishment of a social security, the statutes of autonomy for the regions, and rights such as women's vote or divorce, in a deeply patriarchal society. these reforms became a benchmark for many european countries. it was a reference for democracy in europe, the new frontier of democracy in europe, a democracy that, at that time, was going through difficult times, because it had sunk in italy, in greece, in poland, in hungary and in germany. that is why the military coup not only led to a long and cruel war in spain but also ended the hope for europe that andré malraux had spoken of. the spanish war was not just a war and it was not just spanish. it was a clash between two great world views. yes, the two spaniards of larra and machado were returning, and each spaniard had one of the two spaniards frozen in his heart. but a war between the spaniards would not have been so long, it would not have lasted so long, simply because our own forces would not have allowed it. the war was a defining moment in world history. it had an international significance of enormous magnitude. from 1936 onwards, the future belligerents of europe in world war ii began to directly or indirectly confront each other in the spanish civil war. spain was the first major battle of world war ii, a test bed for a future war that would devastate europe. for the first time in history, the bombing of civilian populations was experienced. guernica is in everyone's memory, but there were many guernica in spain. europeans gave their lives on both sides and their names are on the cemeteries of madrid, jarama, belchite, teruel, guadalajara, the ebro... mythical names, where so many europeans rest and who later walked on the backs of the tanks that covered the geography of european liberation. that war for some was the last great cause, for others it was a crusade. i remember the crusade, the bishops saluting in the fascist fashion, surrounding generals at the entrance of the churches. i also remember the cemeteries full of the shot of both sides. it was the most passionate war, in which the ideologies of the 20th century - democracy, fascism, and communism - first clashed. it was a war of religion and, at the same time, a class struggle, a revolution against a reaction. it was a confrontation that would continue in europe and that also continued in spain, once the war was over, because it was not just a war, there was also a long and hard post-war period, where it was no longer a matter of winning the enemy, since the war had been won, but rather of eradicating it, to maintain a system that remained for a long time and forced spain to remain aloof from the process of democratization and also from the reconstruction that europe experienced, thanks to the marshall plan. many colleagues in the eastern countries remember the isolation they suffered as a result of yalta and the iron curtain that separated them from a free, democratic and prosperous europe, and that is what has happened. but it is less remembered that in southern europe there were countries - spain and portugal - which were also isolated from this movement and remained for a long time under military dictatorships. i remember an american congressman once reproaching me that the europeans were not grateful for the liberation effort which the united states had made with europe. i had to remind him that, as far as spain is concerned, that effort was conspicuous by its absence, because, precisely because the military regime was useful to them in the cold war, they forgot to liberate us. today i would like to make my own the words of salvador de madariaga, whose name is on one of our buildings. before 1936 salvador de madariaga said all spaniards lived in spain and in freedom. today he said in 1954 a few hundred thousand live in freedom, banished from spain and the rest live in spain banished from freedom. freedom returned from 1975. we are beginning to build the foundations of a community based on democracy, freedom and the european perspective. new generations have opened up new political demands with regard to the future and the past. they have found a war and a dictatorship closed and, when today in spain we talk about moral reparation for the victims, what we want to do is discuss the active memory of our country, of our society, to take on the full burden of our past, to honor all the dead, not to discriminate in memory that part that may be uncomfortable for us, not to lock ourselves in the lies that console and to face the truths that illuminate. these are painful wounds that have healed in europe, but which are still in the memory of many people, because they could not exorcise them in their day. that is what gives meaning to an act like today's here in the european parliament, to confront the living past of a part of the memory of our continent, not to repeat yesterday's mistakes, to critically condemn those responsible, to pay tribute to its victims, to express our appreciation to all those who fought for democracy, suffered persecution and promoted the return of spain to europe, as our common homeland. president of the commission. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i think the main points have already been made. but let me make one or two points, particularly by referring to some of the issues raised in the debate. firstly, we are very much in favour of the so-called europe of results approach. but let us be clear: the europe of results is not an alternative to the europe of values, on the contrary, it is the way to strengthen this membership. it is a matter of following two paths at the same time that can reinforce each other. our vision of a europe with concrete projects is based precisely on the idea that we must strengthen the conditions for a europe which has a dimension of social cohesion and justice, a europe which has a political vision, a europe which is ready to use its weight, to exert its influence and to assert its values in the world. that is why we think it is important to go down both paths at the same time. in reply to the question i was asked about the link between enlargement and constitutional reform, i have said it many times: nice is not enough. we need, in an enlarged europe - and we are already an enlarged europe - a reform of the institutions to make them more efficient, more democratic, but also to strengthen the coherence of europe's action in the world. moreover, the constitutional treaty that has been negotiated between the member states has already been negotiated for the europe of twenty-five, reinforcing the idea that a europe of twenty-seven or more will need institutional reform. that is indeed the commission's position. as regards the concrete priorities of this presidency, i would like to stress what has emerged clearly from the debate: the importance attached to innovation. we believe that the lahti summit can be a great moment for europe if indeed the heads of state and government agree now to produce concrete results in the framework of the innovation agenda. as many of you have pointed out here today, europe has excellent universities and excellent research centres, but it lacks the capacity to translate all this activity into more concrete results for the economy and for the competitiveness of our continent. we must therefore improve the link between knowledge, science and research on the one hand and practical results on the other. innovation is the key to this. finland, with its experience and specific vocation, can help us to achieve these concrete results. another area in which our action will be judged at the end of these six months is justice, security and freedom. this debate has clearly shown a broad support for the idea that we must do more at community level too. there is of course an intergovernmental dimension, more can be done in terms of intergovernmental cooperation, but we need a community dimension in certain areas, for example the management of immigration, legal or illegal. the problems facing some of our member states today, spain for example, are not just their own problems, they are problems facing the whole of europe. it is clear that in these circumstances we cannot separate legal immigration from illegal immigration and that we need a european approach in this area. i believe that in this area we will all be judged at the end of this semester, the finnish presidency, we member states, on our willingness to produce, on the basis of the existing treaties, more results in the area of justice and security, including, of course, immigration. another issue which is a high priority for this parliament, and which is also a priority for the finnish presidency, is energy. we must be clear on this, particularly in relation to relations with russia. firstly, we are in favour of a constructive partnership with russia in the field of energy, but what we are proposing - and this was clearly stated in the strategy paper that the commission produced - is not just to develop good relations with russia, it is diversification. the solution to europe's energy problem is diversification: diversification of the country of origin, of the country of supply, diversification of the countries of transit and also diversification of energy sources, in particular by increasing investment in renewable energies. so the solution for energy is diversification and not to lock ourselves into a relationship with one partner, however important that partner may be. secondly, let us be clear about relations with russia. in the negotiating mandate for our relations with that country which we have presented to the council, the first point that appears is not energy, it is not even trade, no, the first point concerns human rights, respect for democracy, respect for the principles of the rule of law. this is the condition for developing a special partnership with a country with which we of course want to develop our relations, a country which also wants to develop its relations with us. a final point, if i may, on the continuity of which prime minister vanhanen has spoken very well. it is true that we, the european parliament and the commission, have a five-year mandate and that the various presidencies each have a specific vocation, but there is sometimes a problem of continuity over time, which was also identified during the negotiations on the constitutional treaty. i believe that we are beginning to make progress on mr president, i speak on behalf of the socialist group to put the question put by mr schulz and mr roure on behalf of the socialist group. this question is in addition to the reports drawn up by mr gaubert and mr lambrinidis on immigration issues. i would point out that these two reports make an important contribution to the problem of immigration. the fundamental concern is that there should be a comprehensive immigration policy. we have only fragments of policies so far, and let us hope that the resolutions of the last brussels summit will enable us to make such a comprehensive policy. but comprehensive immigration policy has to start with the countries of origin. i mean, what are we doing in the european union to prevent immigration from being, in many of these countries, the only source of income for their inhabitants? this is the first thing we have to consider. secondly, on the basis that the problems of developing countries cannot be solved in the short term, what measures are we taking to protect our external borders, including, of course, a legal immigration policy - which has been included in the hague programme since december 2005 - so that those citizens who want to come to work in our union, if there are jobs available, can do so legally? thirdly, it must be remembered - as has just been said in previous reports - that at present, in the absence of a union policy on immigration, each country has to bear the costs and the efforts of that policy. at the moment there are a number of border countries, not only in southern europe but also in central europe, which are bearing an excessive burden in terms of the humanitarian attention to be given to these illegal immigrants. so far, the means at our disposal have been minimal. it seems that we have only about 5 700 000 euro available for this year. we hope that with the adoption of the financial perspective, as from 1 january 2007, we will have additional resources. we must also bear in mind that these immigrants are not extraterrestrial beings, not robots, not machines, but people who have to live in society, who have family and emotional needs that must be met. and above all, what europe cannot allow is that there are two kinds of citizens within it: those who - as a section of the french far right has said - are of souche, that is, of european origin, and those who are not, because that, as we have seen recently, is the source of a number of social problems which are very difficult to solve. we must integrate immigrants into our societies. they cannot be kept out of the mainstream of our society. an immigrant, the children of immigrants and the grandchildren of immigrants have the right to live as persons on an equal footing with other citizens of the union. it is also important to remember that the flow of immigration does not have to be completely irreversible. the heart of every immigrant harbors the desire to return to his country of origin. what are we doing to ensure that immigrants have the possibility of maintaining a link with their country of origin, that they can return to their country of origin without having to resort to these horrible illegal immigration procedures, that their stay outside their country of origin is regarded as nothing more than a transitional stage, so that when they return they can enrich the society of their country of origin? it is something that in some countries of the european union, such as spain, italy, portugal and greece, was done at a time when staying abroad was simply a procedure to return to one's country of origin and strengthen its economy. i hope that commissioner frattini will help us in this respect - we have a great task ahead of us - and that the institutions of the union, the commission, the council and parliament, will be able to develop this necessary immigration policy, which is so essential at this time.
mr president, mr frattini, i congratulate you, but only you. let us look at some of the aspects identified. the european union is aware of the problem and is alarmed by every visible crisis: lampedusa, ceuta, melilla, malta and the canary islands. but it does not have the common policies needed to prevent or manage migration flows properly, neither legal nor, much less, illegal. the countries of the south add drama to the pressure and the violation of the union's borders. the dead are so many that they cannot be quantified with precision. i have said a thousand times that this great question has five essential aspects which are interrelated: legal immigration, illegal immigration, asylum, integration and subsidiary protection. this includes the causes, both remote and immediate: origin and transit, structural poverty and the irresponsible calls which are translated into all the poor languages with the dangerous phrase 'at the end, sooner or later, paper for all'. and in the meantime, how do we witness this spectacle of incompetence and incapacity? i'll give you two examples; i'll tell you what's going to happen this weekend. tomorrow and the day after tomorrow in brussels the council at technical level will say that it has begun to discuss the breakdown by country of the three new integration funds: border control, illegal repatriation and integration. but what's the matter? meanwhile, spain, greece and the netherlands are fighting over the criteria for allocation: migratory pressure, border kilometres or number of air entries. we are not discussing funds, we are discussing little funds. this morning, mr millán mon said that in the financial perspective, only 50 cents out of every 100 euros is allocated to immigration. that's the big tip. that is the great truth. another negative example, mr president, is that the council - which i strongly criticise - will also be responding to this by adopting a comprehensive approach to immigration the day after tomorrow. that is all the council will be proposing: a global approach. finally, mr frattini, it is very important to involve the countries of origin and the countries of transit, it is very important that mr solana goes to those countries of origin and those countries of transit. frontex is not the answer. frontex is a newborn baby. frontex will not do anything without the carabinieri or the civil guard. so no complacency and all the common demand in the face of this very serious problem.

ladies and gentlemen, since we parted company before the summer, there have been a number of events which i would like to mention in order to give you an idea of our work and to inform you of the activities of the parliamentary bodies which have taken place during the summer. firstly, with regard to the war in lebanon: in the face of the tragic events that were taking place, i felt that parliament could not remain on holiday and had to react. a special conference of presidents of political groups was therefore convened on 20 july. the conference of presidents adopted a clear and much more forceful declaration than that of the union's foreign affairs council on the 17th, in which we called for an immediate ceasefire in the region; we were also the first to call for the deployment of an international force within the framework of the united nations and with a strong participation of the european union. the presidents of the political groups unanimously called for the institutions of the union and its member states to speak with one voice, which unfortunately did not happen. on 1 august, in the face of the continuing escalation of violence and attacks against civilians, the conference of presidents held a new extraordinary meeting, this time open to all members. the conference of presidents clearly condemned attacks against civilians, such as those which had just taken place in the lebanese city of qana. we again appealed to the council to call for an immediate ceasefire. in accordance with the resolutions of this conference of presidents, i negotiated a declaration by the bureau of the euro-mediterranean parliamentary assembly which was published on 7 august. it was the first time that european and arab political leaders had spoken with one voice in relation to this crisis. on 24 august the apem bureau met in brussels, having previously convened all the members of the european parliament who are members of this house. the apem bureau adopted a declaration calling for european participation in the intervention force and decided to send a delegation to lebanon, israel and the palestinian territories. finally, on 25 august, as you know, the governments of the member states decided to respond to our calls for action and to those also addressed to them by the united nations, by sending a considerable contingent of troops from european countries to the area. as you can understand, these meetings have had to be called at very short notice and not all members who had decided or wished to participate in them were able to hear about them in time. i apologize for the rush in the timing of these meetings and i am therefore also glad that we are including a debate on this matter on the first agenda. it is clear to everyone that the european union is undertaking the largest military mission ever undertaken, that it is a challenge to our political credibility and that beyond the role of peacekeepers in an area which affects us very directly, the union has the opportunity to support diplomatic action in the region as a whole and to relaunch the peace process between israel and palestine. the second theme of the summer was the influx of illegal immigrants from africa, particularly to the coasts of the canary islands and lampedusa. i have been in constant contact with commissioner frattini, whom i would like to thank for the decisions he has taken and the impetus he has given to cooperation between european countries to resolve some cases, particularly dramatic from a humanitarian point of view, relating to illegal immigration. but let us be aware that this summer 10 000 people have arrived in lampedusa and 20 000 in the canary islands, almost 2 000 more yesterday alone, that is to say four times as many as last year, and hundreds of people have died at sea trying to cross. let us also be aware that these people do not want to stay on lampedusa or lanzarote, they want to go to europe. what is happening there therefore affects us all, it affects europe as a whole, both in its immigration policy and in its development policy. i would like to draw the attention of parliament, of all of us, to the fact that we are not facing an emergency, we are not facing an exceptional problem that occurs once in a while: we are facing a structural problem that is going to recur more strongly every summer because the income and demographic differential between europe and africa will cause this immigration to increase, and in the face of this europe must put in place a policy of development in africa and cooperation between european countries, developing for this purpose a common immigration policy. finally, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to point out, as you know, that the summer was also marked by the preparation of a major attack on the air routes linking the united kingdom and the united states, which reminds us of the continuing terrorist threat. we are also reminded of the deadly attacks in turkey, which have claimed the lives of european citizens. this must increase our efforts to deal with the phenomenon of terrorism by means acceptable to us and respectful of our freedoms. the commission's vice-president mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i am pleased to present to you today the proposal for a regulation on the financing of measures to combat pollution caused by ships. the purpose of this regulation is to provide the european maritime safety agency with the financial means it needs to carry out the new tasks assigned to it in the field of the fight against pollution caused by ships. since the agency's responsibility for pollution control is intended to be exercised in the long term, this text defines a financial envelope to be charged to the community budget on the basis of a multiannual commitment. the effective performance of the tasks is only possible if there is financial security based on a multiannual commitment. the purpose of the proposal is therefore to lay down the procedures for the community contribution, set at eur 154 million 2004 reference amount for the period 2007-13. the proposal provides that the financial means made available to the agency are to cover all the pollution control activities of the agency as listed in its action plan adopted in october 2004. among these activities, i would particularly highlight operational assistance to member states wishing to strengthen national pollution response mechanisms by means of specialised vessels: in fact reserve vessels equipped for the recovery of pollutants at sea which the agency will make available to member states. another activity was the development, in addition to aerial surveillance, of a satellite imaging service to enable pollution to be detected and thus assist the member states in their fight against illicit discharges and accidental spills of hydrocarbons. another activity is the development of a capacity to react to accidents involving harmful and dangerous substances. i thank your rapporteur and the committee on transport and tourism for seeking and succeeding, mr president, in reaching agreement with the council at first reading. this constructive approach between the two institutions should make it possible to adopt the regulation quickly, so that a viable system for combating pollution at community level can be established without delay. i would like to thank mr luis de grandes pascual and the committee on transport and tourism for their work. the compromise you have reached clarifies the commission's proposal on a number of points. the commission therefore fully supports and accepts all the compromise amendments proposed by parliament. i thank you for your attention and will now follow closely the sensible remarks of the various speakers.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the transport sector is not left behind. i have tried to reach basic consensus through dialogue with all those who have shown an interest in this work. at the same time, as you have said, mr commissioner, we have had a fluid and fruitful relationship with the commission and the council, which has resulted in compromise amendments which will allow this report to be adopted at first reading and, consequently, to avoid delay in the measures envisaged in the context of the new tasks entrusted to the agency, to combat pollution from ships more effectively. i shall briefly outline the main features of the report. firstly, it is a financial regulation, which allows the agency to carry out the new tasks assigned to it on the basis of a seven-year multiannual commitment, covering the period 2007-2013, in accordance with the new financial perspective. the new tasks assigned to the agency are aimed at increasing maritime safety and preventing pollution from ships in the waters of the member states. the commission initially set the amount of the commitment at eur 154 million, an amount which was consolidated by parliament in the financial perspective and which has been maintained without any reduction in the interinstitutional agreement reached last may. it should be noted that this amount was originally indicative and has now been agreed by parliament, the council and the commission. this is the minimum staff needed to carry out the new tasks assigned to the agency. it should be recalled that the purpose of the agency is to provide the appropriate framework for the development of concrete actions to increase maritime safety and prevent pollution by ships in the waters of the member states, and to provide the states with additional means when national response means are insufficient to deal with a large-scale disaster. it must therefore be stressed that the agency is not intended to replace the action of the member states, but to make up for the lack of resources of the states affected by disasters and to complement their action. the additional means in question are essentially long-term chartering of vessels through availability contracts with commercial shipowners who have vessels with sufficient capacity to adapt to pollution control operations. in response to a request for assistance from a member state, these vessels would interrupt their usual commercial activities in order to deploy in the disaster area. as regards the criteria for selecting priorities for the deployment of vessels by zone, as a result of the amendments submitted and the agreements reached with the council, the agency should pay particular attention to the areas declared to be more vulnerable, as they are susceptible to a higher risk of accident or deliberate spillage given their characteristics and precedents, without prejudice to the possibility of providing assistance in any other area within community waters that needs and requests assistance. in 2005, the first contract for support vessels - a total of seven - for oil recovery was awarded by means of a restricted tender. before the end of this year, 2006, the second tender will be closed. the agency is now seeking to award four new contracts for vessels, covering preferably the two large atlantic areas and the mediterranean area. the rapporteur believes that this should be the occasion to fulfil the commitment made to galicia. in any event, before the agency starts to contract support vessels, it shall first take stock of the means available to the member states in order to optimise in complementary terms the needs of the member states which the agency is to serve. it should also be noted that the rapporteur's aim of extending the scope of the regulation so that the agency's actions take account not only of pollution by oil but also of pollution by harmful and dangerous substances has been achieved. on this point, consensus has been reached by using the term 'pollution from ships' to describe pollution caused not only by oil but also by harmful and dangerous substances. it is also worth noting that it was agreed that the agency would play an important role in the development of a centralised satellite imagery service for monitoring, early detection of pollution and identification of ships responsible, increasing the availability of data and efficiency in the fight against marine pollution. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union's institutions. we have noted that in the past other agencies have been accused of acting with a certain opacity and away from parliamentary control. in order to avoid such detrimental features, it has been agreed that, independently of the four-yearly evaluation provided for in article 7, the european parliament will be regularly informed on the financial implementation of the resources allocated to the agency. ladies and gentlemen, we are convinced that the new practices of transparency will enhance the prestige of the agency, and will remove from it any image of a mere bureaucratic instrument. i would like to conclude, ladies and gentlemen, by asking for support for this report, which is not the work of this rapporteur alone, but the result of the involvement of all the political groups and the consensus between parliament, the commission and the council.
on behalf of the alde group. mr president, commissioner, the european maritime safety agency is ready to get involved in the fight against marine pollution from the thousands of ships that ply the community's waters every day, but it must be acknowledged beforehand that there is an inability of the member states to respond to the great ecological disasters we suffer from time to time, such as the sadly remembered cases of the shipwreck of the erika and, above all, the prestige. it is right to recognize that it cannot be required that each and every coastal member state, regardless of its size and wealth, should be permanently equipped with sufficient physical and technological means to respond immediately and effectively to major accidents and disasters. it should also be noted that ships transport goods and merchandise which not only originate and are destined for coastal states but which are also part of the supply and trade chain of other continental or non-maritime states and therefore share a share of the risks of maritime transport. it is therefore appropriate and necessary to adopt community measures to supplement and support those established by the individual member states, without thereby relieving the latter of their primary responsibility both in preventing and responding to marine pollution. among those support measures, the european maritime safety agency shall establish a system for the collection and analysis of information on pollution from ships, which would include satellite photographic monitoring, scientific and technical assistance and operational assistance, by vessels distributed over various maritime geographical regions and ready to intervene in the event of accidents and disasters at the request of the member states concerned. numerous and harmful.

budget for 2006. this has allowed the commission to launch an initiative to design, develop and test european approaches to joint civil protection intervention. this cooperation and coordination will make our fight against natural disasters – such as the floods in several european countries, or the summer forest fires in spain, for which assistance was requested by the spanish authorities on 9 august – even more effective. on the specific question of forest fires, which was raised by a number of members, it is necessary to note as i have before that forestry matters are a member state competence. member states are responsible for launching actions to protect forests threatened by fire, as well as restoration efforts. the main aim of the measures we take at european union level is to reinforce the member states’ policies. these measures include the possibility of financial support available under the new rural development regulation, the forest focus regulation and, from 2007, the commission’s proposal for life plus, which explicitly provides for the possibility of financing forest monitoring programmes and forest fire prevention activities in order to continue the work of the forest forum. let us look towards the future. the commission is preparing a study to look at the effectiveness of community measures for forest protection and at options to improve the effectiveness of these measures. the results of these analyses are expected by the end of 2007. the commission has proposed a directive under the codecision procedure on the assessment and management of floods, which i hope will be adopted soon. the commission has also undertaken preparatory work with regard to the threat of droughts, which become more intensive and frequent each year, particularly, but not only, in the southern parts of europe. we are engaged in discussions with the member states to collect information and to assess whether similar legislative action is needed. quite a few speakers referred to the council regulation establishing the european union solidarity fund, which does not allow the commission to mobilise the fund on its own initiative. it is necessary for the member state concerned to make an application to the commission within ten weeks of the date of the first damage. to date, no such application has been received from the spanish government. the possibility of financial assistance from the solidarity fund depends on whether the criteria in the regulation for mobilising the fund are met. the rules governing this instrument allow for the possibility of assistance in the event of major natural disasters. to qualify for aid, the estimated cost of total direct damage must exceed eur 3 billion at 2002 prices, or 0.6% of gross national income of the state in question, whichever is lower. the solidarity fund is not designed to support general longer-term prevention measures for the rehabilitation of agricultural production potential. in such cases, other potential sources of funding exist at community level, including projects co-financed by the structural funds. in addition, several possibilities of response to national disaster exist within the common agricultural policy. in 2006, the commission’s civil protection mechanism responded to floods, earthquakes, forest fires, marine pollution and emergencies with a humanitarian dimension. four european countries requested assistance in the spring floods, even though a greater number were eventually affected. we sent experts to all sorts of situations, from coordinating the european effort in cyprus and lebanon to assisting the indonesian authorities in the aftermath of the earthquake and the eruption of a volcano. we sent emergency supplies such as medicines, medical supplies, food and shelter. we dispatched equipment to pump water and to extinguish fires. with your support we shall continue to better prepare ourselves and to improve our response for the benefit of the member states and those we seek to help.

member states in combating the threat of terrorism is essential, as is effective cooperation with third countries. the link between human rights, development and security is essential for comprehensive security and its global consolidation. the european union's security strategy is based on this premise, which was adopted at the united nations. we can make a difference by our actions in creating a more just world and in the achievement of the un millennium development goals. the union's strength lies in the wide range of instruments at its disposal, from humanitarian aid to agricultural, trade, development and environmental policies. eu development policy can also be seen as part of eu security policy. the eu is the largest development and trade partner of developing countries and the world's largest donor of development aid. i hope and believe that the eu institutions will reach a decision on development finance in good cooperation, in order to ensure uninterrupted eu funding and, in particular, the eu's multifaceted action, also from the beginning of 2007. there is a link between development and trade. it is not always automatically positive, but it requires political will and skill. trade can thus be brought to bear on the economic growth, poverty reduction and social development of developing countries. but developing countries themselves must also be prepared to implement national reforms, promote good governance and crack down on corruption. market access alone may not be enough for a fairer globalisation, but special measures to strengthen the capacity of the poorest countries are also needed to support them. a joint meeting of trade and development ministers will be held in october to secure a strong eu commitment to the world trade organisation's aid for trade recommendations and their rapid implementation. the same broad and varied treatment is required for the cross-border movement of people. i believe that this is already being discussed in finland at the lahti summit. i also believe that we are ready to move forward with the decision-making process in december. human rights are a sensitive subject: we have accepted their legal and ethical bindingness, but their consolidation in practical policy is a very challenging task. the european union's human rights policy must, however, be based on the same rules in all parts of the world. fortunately, we also have good partners, first and foremost, of course, the united nations. in europe, the council of europe is an important partner for us, whose expertise we must make better use of. the eu's accession to the european convention on human rights remains an important objective. the report by the prime minister of luxembourg, jean-claude juncker, contains excellent proposals for closer cooperation between the two organisations, but the implementation of this report needs to be worked on. the union has become increasingly concerned both with conflict prevention and with crisis management itself. you'll have to allow me to be a little nostalgic. when i was finland's foreign minister and i took the initiative with my swedish colleague lena hjelm-wallén to develop the eu's crisis management capacity, we certainly did not dare to hope for very rapid progress. but it didn't. the initiative was adopted by the treaty of amsterdam and today the cornerstone of the union's rapidly evolving crisis management policy is the development and effective coordination of military and civilian activities. the most sustainable way to resolve conflicts is to engage widely. for example, the need to send an eu crisis management team to the democratic republic of congo in support of the un has already been demonstrated when violent clashes broke out after the first round of elections. i hope that the situation will remain stable so that the campaign and the second round of elections can proceed peacefully and with respect for democracy. after the elections, the country must move quickly into a phase of reconstruction and development. the eu is already working to reform the country's security sector. the european union is also actively working to resolve the difficult situation in darfur. the union is the largest contributor to the african union peacekeeping mission amis. the decisions to strengthen the peacekeeping mission and transfer it to the un must be implemented swiftly, because the human suffering in the region must not be allowed to continue. the european union's international action is therefore increasingly expected. the union as a whole is a strong actor, as the situation in lebanon has shown. the eu has been active in promoting a political solution, first in the formulation of un security council resolution 1701 and now in its full implementation. it is, however, essential that the parties remain committed to the implementation of the resolution. the union's determined action has strengthened confidence in the eu as a mediator of peace in the region. we cannot of course do this alone, but the european union can play a very important role. the member states of the european union have taken on a major role in the un extended mission unifil, which supports the fragile ceasefire and the efforts to achieve lasting peace throughout the region. the decision to assume responsibility at the extraordinary general affairs and external relations council on 25 august was a turning point in the strengthening of unifil. the member states were able to take decisions which are very demanding at national level. the union's member states have committed themselves to deploying around 7 000 peacekeepers to the unifil operation. the entire un operation is being led by europeans, first in france and then in italy. it is important, however, that the range of countries sending troops to the operation is wider than the european union. this will ensure the confidence of the parties in the execution of the operation. the situation in lebanon is a whole which is not only a security problem but also a political, economic and social problem. we must support the strengthening of the lebanese government, its extension of power to the whole of lebanon and its assumption of responsibility for the reconstruction process. the total amount of assistance from the european commission and the member states to improve the difficult humanitarian situation in lebanon has already exceeded eur 300 million. the conference on the humanitarian situation in lebanon and also in the palestinian territories held in stockholm at the end of last week was a real success. the amount of aid granted and new commitments to provide aid is substantial. in addition to immediate humanitarian aid, the union will have a major role to play in reconstruction and environmental remediation. lasting peace in the middle east requires a solution to the conflict between israel and the palestinians. the eu played a key role in the development of the roadmap and now it must take the lead in promoting a comprehensive peace plan. everyone must commit to the two-state model of security and viability. trust also needs to be built at the level of civil society, not just between governments, which is of course important in itself. i believe that if women are strongly involved in the peace process, the chances of a lasting solution will increase. i have already worked with unifem, the un women's fund, which supports dialogue between israeli and palestinian women. we will also be raising this issue at the next un general assembly week. you will be coming to the plenary tomorrow to discuss the middle east in a broad way. it is essential that the european union continues to be determined in the pursuit of stability and security throughout the middle east. the middle east is our neighborhood. eu representatives have taken the initiative in negotiations on iran's nuclear programme. iran must comply with the un security council resolution and seize the opportunity for genuine dialogue now. in the coming weeks and months, the eu must continue its vigorous and comprehensive diplomacy across the region. the united states is a key partner for the eu in this, not to mention the other permanent members of the security council. the destinies of russia and the rest of europe have been intertwined for centuries. today russia is a strategic partner of the eu. the russian leadership has repeatedly stated that its european choice is irreversible. the eu and russia have agreed to cooperate on a wide range of issues, including trade and human rights, which will benefit both parties and also support the development of democracy and stability in russia. recently, energy issues have been particularly high on the agenda. it is good that the eu is seeking a common approach to energy issues, even though the choice of energy sources is a national matter. however, there are many areas where cooperation is essential. the eu's external relations must be more closely linked to energy policy so that the union's external relations can support energy security. i believe that this is the area where the union's positive interdependence with russia can be particularly evident. this eu-russia energy dialogue must be based on trust. we must try to find common interests. we must also all work together to combat climate change by reducing emissions, conserving energy, developing cleaner technologies and promoting the use of renewable energy sources. we know that the energy resources available today are not limitless. the eu must also seek to establish a broad cooperation with russia in the environmental sector. the union and russia have a comprehensive partnership and cooperation agreement, complemented by road maps in four mutually agreed areas. these are the economy, freedom, justice and security, external security and research, education and culture. the latter are not insignificant areas of cooperation, although they do not appear in public so often. for example, student exchanges and getting to know each other's cultures are practical ways of getting to know each other better. the eu-russia partnership and cooperation agreement is due to expire at the end of next year. our aim is to be able to agree at the eu-russia summit in november to open negotiations with russia to renew the treaty arrangements. i also believe that the renewal of the northern dimension as a common policy of the eu, russia, norway and iceland will further strengthen our relations with these partner countries. the northern dimension focuses in particular on environmental cooperation and social and health issues. the enlargement of the union has contributed to stability and security in europe and has brought economic benefits to all member states, old and new. successful enlargement also strengthens the eu's international role. i believe that the european union must remain open to all european countries which fulfil the conditions for membership. the development the countries of central europe, turkey, croatia and the western balkans are clear examples of the strong incentive for reform from the perspective of eu membership, although of course the ultimate objective of change in each country must be the desire to improve the daily life and security of its citizens. people also value membership through their everyday experiences. the december european council will hold a general debate on enlargement. we will then look together at how the enlargement process is being carried forward. as you know, the european council held a debate in june on the capacity of the union to receive refugees. the result was that no new criteria for membership should be set, but the existing ones should be strictly adhered to. it is in the interests of both the european union and the applicant countries that accession to the union should only take place when the applicant country is able to assume the obligations of membership and to fulfil the conditions of membership. we must, for our part, honour the commitments we have made to the applicant countries and ensure our capacity to welcome new member states. it is also important to remember what is not included in the requirements. we share common values, but we're not trying to be one culture. on the contrary, the richness and strength of europe lies in its cultural diversity. different political views are a natural part of europe. you and your political groups are a unique example of cross-border cooperation between national political groups. a multiform union needs a multi-dimensional parliamentarism. i have spoken to you at length and i know that we all have a busy autumn, both in this parliament and in our presidency and in the other member states. this week, the eu-asia summit on asem is being held in finland. the asem has already become a de facto cooperation between two regional groups, and working with an integrated union has also encouraged closer coordination between asian countries in preparing matters. i think it is clear to all of us that 'global before we move on to the next item on the agenda, i must make a communication to the house. you will recall that we have sometimes had disagreements on the interpretation of rule 166 of our rules of procedure and that some members felt that the presidency was not making proper use of it, as it did not allow the floor for points of order which did not relate to the subject under discussion at the time. article 166 does not clearly specify whether the allowance to speak on a point of order must refer to the subject under debate or to the agenda for that day, or whether it may refer to any other subject. however, in the president's view, it should be common sense to say that concessions of the floor could only be made on the basis of the subject under discussion and not on any other. however, in order to settle the controversy which had arisen at certain points in the chamber, i asked the committee on constitutional affairs for its opinion, which, in its reply, proposed the following interpretation of rule 166: 'requests for the floor to comment on the observance of the rules of procedure must refer to the item on the agenda currently being debated. the president may grant the floor on another matter at an appropriate time, for example, after the conclusion of the debate on an item on the agenda or before the sitting is adjourned. it is therefore clear from now on that the correct interpretation is the one indicated by common sense and that rule 166 can only be invoked to make observations on compliance with the rules of procedure relating to the item on the agenda which is being discussed at that moment. i would remind you that the interpretation of the committee on constitutional affairs is deemed to have been adopted if it is not challenged before the minutes of this sitting are adopted.

the next item is the report by mrs carmen fraga estévez, on behalf of the committee on fisheries, on launching a debate on a community approach to the labelling systems for fishery products (2005/2189 (ini)) (a6-0219/2006).
the first thing i would like to stress, as rapporteur for this report, is the indisputable role that a credible label or certification can play, among the measures that can be taken, in trying to ensure sustainable fishing. however, the matter has been on the european commission's table since the 1990s, and until now no one has decided to tackle it. in the meantime, with the market becoming increasingly aware of environmental issues, private promoters of fisheries eco-labels are making their move, causing total confusion among consumers, at best, and more than likely discrediting the system in general, because when you can apply a surplus value to a product by saying it is ecological, without having to prove it, the way to fraud is served. i am one of those who have on many occasions reminded the commission that it should address this matter as soon as possible. that is why many of us were disappointed when the commission finally published this communication, a document which was almost devoid of content, lacked analysis, made no commitments and did not provide any criteria or guidelines to follow. it is clear that this result was achieved in less than ten years and that the commission is completely overwhelmed by the reality of the attractive eco-label market and the many and varied interests which support it, some of them very much to be applauded, others not so much. in this connection, i would like to recall that, in his appearance before the committee on fisheries on the occasion of his dismissal, former commissioner fischler confessed that the unfinished business of his mandate had been that he had not been able to deal with a regulation on eco-labelling and that, i quote, 'due to the many pressures received'. the commission has also proposed that the criteria for defining sustainable fishery products be established in a sound manner. but we must do it because other interested parties are doing it for us and many are doing it for their own interests. the commission is not alone in this task either, because it already has guidelines on this from the fao and discussions in a wide variety of international forums, including the world trade organization. governments, ngos, private companies and fishermen also contributed their views. and in this report, with the invaluable and varied contributions of many colleagues, including those from the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, the european parliament is also making its contribution to defining the lines that will allow consumers, politicians and the fishing industry to become more involved in the sustainability of fisheries resources. we believe that, on the whole, a community labelling system must be consistent with the existing guidelines of international bodies, that it must not lead to any discrimination, that it must not create obstacles to trade, particularly for the least developed countries, and that it must be a weapon in the fight against illegal fishing by preventing access to markets. as regards its internal functioning, the committee on fisheries considers that, irrespective of the fact that there may be one or more labels, which are always voluntary, the system should be unique and promoted by the european union, which should establish its operating rules and ensure the independence of the accreditation and certification bodies, as well as the transparency and veracity of information at all stages of the chain of custody, from the fishing vessel to the final consumer. we also ask the commission to submit a communication within six months on the minimum requirements and guidelines to be met by a community system of labelling fishery products, and i would add that it should clarify whether the commission is finally inclined to call it an eco-label, or what other name it chooses and why, and we urge it to take account of the reflections put to it by this house.
on behalf of the pse group. mr president, i would like to congratulate mrs fraga on the interesting report we are debating in this house today. the in-depth study of consumer preferences and attitudes is a basic need for any industry, and it is obviously the same for fishery products. changing lifestyles and the introduction of new technologies have changed the european consumer, who is increasingly concerned about his health and also about the protection of the environment. one of the best methods of providing information is labelling, which must therefore be clear and understandable and contain truthful information. for this reason, i am glad that the commission is finally taking up this debate on the labelling systems for fishery products in order to define the approach to be taken on this issue from the european union. the fact is that the growing importance which consumers attach to sustainable development has given rise to a bewildering collection of private labels, without any control, which can distort their original purpose, namely to guarantee an environmentally friendly catch and processing system. if, in addition, additional information is provided on the sustainability of the product, the independence of the inspection and accreditation body must be guaranteed, as the rapporteur rightly points out. in this respect, i take up the words of the director-general of fisheries markets and structures in spain, alberto lópez, when he points out the need to avoid the trivialization of eco-labelling. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the labels are not subject to homogeneous and accredited standards. in this respect, i cannot but welcome the fao's initiative to audit all eco-labels to identify those with technical and scientific backing and to seek coherence and harmonisation. the committee on fisheries shares the commission's objectives, such as sustainability and the need for european action in this area.

member of the commission. mr president, first of all i would like to thank the rapporteur, mrs fraga estévez, and everyone who has spoken tonight. although not in agreement on all aspects, the commission and parliament are on the same wavelength as regards moving towards adopting decisions based on tariff assessments and broad consultations. i would underline to the last speaker, mr nicholson, that the debate tonight fully reflects the way the commission wanted to involve parliament before entering the legislative phase of what needs to be done on eco-labelling. obviously, when it comes to that legislative phase, the involvement of parliament will be a top priority prior to finalisation of the whole process relating to the eco-labelling scheme. let me refer to some specific points that were raised during the debate. most of the existing schemes are in effect relatively consistent and are not misleading. the commission’s preferred option for establishing minimum criteria for eco-labelling schemes will, however, bring order to the system, where necessary, and increase consumer confidence. we will also be ensuring better quality products and providing for transparency and the traceability of products on the market. on the point raised by various speakers on the preference for a single eco-labelling scheme, it is still early to take a definitive and final decision. the commission has, however, indicated its preferred option and i should underline that the economic and social committee, the advisory committee on fisheries and agriculture, and most industry and stakeholders’ representatives support that option. however, although a preference for option 3 - the commission’s preferred option - which is to say the setting of minimum criteria, seems to be emerging, no agreement has yet been reached between member states at council level. that is why i underline the fact that it is still too early to take a firm and definitive stand on how to proceed. however, this debate has certainly helped to better inform us on parliament’s position and on that of its various members. on the issue of the harvesting of fisheries resources in a sustainable way, i wish to refer to the commission’s communication, which underlines that the aim of the policy on eco-labelling for fish and fisheries products is based on the concept of sustainable fishing. the communications spells out that eco-labelling schemes, if based on clearly-defined criteria and appropriate indicators, can assist in both monitoring the progress made on sustainability in fishing and in raising public awareness on sustainability issues. it goes on to make reference to sustainable exploitation with regard to article 3(e) of council regulation (ec) no 2371/2002. regarding the other points raised, i agree with the comments on the importance of independent accreditation and certification. guarantees in this area are provided by iso standards and procedures. however, the commission has no direct competence to enforce those norms. i also agree with the comments made to the effect that eco-labelling needs to be clear and clearly understandable so that it is easily understood by consumers. moreover, eco-labels offer the possibility of helping to combat iuu fishing and of promoting proof with regard to sustainable fishing practices. by virtue of the whole exercise undertaken, we will be increasing awareness among the general public. fao criteria will be taken into account when it comes to laying the basis of eco-labelling schemes. moreover, the schemes must not be cumbersome to smes, or so complex that they cannot be effectively implemented by stakeholders.

on behalf of the pse group. mr president, after the intervention of commissioner frattini, it seems that we have achieved the objective we set ourselves with this exercise, despite the late hour. finally, the commissioner told us that this possibility of parliament's participation in the procedure for adopting conventions by the hague conference is enshrined in the framework agreement on the institutions and that the european parliament could therefore formally take part in these negotiations. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the establishment of a european union agency for the evaluation of medicinal products. i think we should start by thanking the commissioner for his generous words, because there is no legal obligation. i would also like to add my voice to those of my predecessors who have said that judicial cooperation in civil matters is now a competence of the european union under the treaty of amsterdam and that we also have the hague programme for the development of judicial cooperation in civil matters. this is not a peripheral area in relation to the very essence of the european union, but a central area, which means that the three institutions will have to work together on this matter, so it is quite appropriate to work together. in the motion for a resolution tabled by mr gargani on behalf of the committee on legal affairs, there is also another rather interesting suggestion, namely that it is not only a question of the european parliament cooperating with the commission in the negotiations to be held at the hague conference, but also that a sort of parliamentary forum should be created - which would be a task which this parliament could take on by meeting with national parliamentarians. in short, european union law on private matters is still largely national law and the creation of such a parliamentary forum would therefore allow us to harmonize positions. the great problem in private international law, as we all know, and in private law in general, is that these are national rights, which even correspond to different traditions. but at a time when we are thinking of harmonizing, codifying or unifying private law, the creation of such a parliamentary forum, perhaps for this specific purpose for now, would be a good principle so that the european institutions do not appear to be unconnected with national legal traditions. those of us who have worked in this field have seen the enormous difficulties that exist in making any progress in the area of private law, because of the differences between national traditions, but this proposal, which is more directed at parliament itself than at the commission, would be very positive, because it would enable us to harmonize positions with the national parliaments and bring those harmonized positions to the conference, through our participation in it.
on behalf of the alde group. mr president, what we are discussing today is really a sign of the european union's maturity. not so many years ago, when i was meeting with other people who were teaching private international law in different universities, to mix private international law or private law with european union law was a heresy, because, quite simply, the european union was concerned with fisheries, at most, international trade and competition, but it was not really concerned with private law issues. today the european union has much to say in the field of private law, because today, although we still have a long way to go, the european union is already dealing with the private consequences of european citizenship, its direct impact on the private space of individuals and the consequences that freedom of establishment and movement has on the private law of individuals and companies. all this was the impetus for the introduction of this subject in the amsterdam treaty and for the development of the european union - the european community, to be precise - to have these powers, which have made it possible to draw up a large number of legislation or to convert into european legislation instruments which were not, although they were, in some way, part of the community, such as the brussels convention and others. in this context, therefore, the accession of the european union - the community in the strict sense - to the hague conference is a very important step and shows, i repeat, the maturity of the european union; it shows that we still have a long way to go, inter alia, as regards the way in which these rules are drawn up: third pillar, first pillar, etc. it is not the time to discuss it, but it is something which will result in improving the quality of our own legislation and which will certainly allow the european union to bring its own priorities to the hague conference. so, even though it is midnight and there are very few people here, this is a real test and an indication of the maturity of the european union in areas which affect the citizen very directly.

that ‘despite some promising initiatives on mobility and participation in eu programmes, there is still a lack of national strategies on the european dimension in education’. policies that would ensure that, after initial education, young people have the knowledge and competences they need as european citizens – not only as tourists but as citizens – are piecemeal and fragmented. it is also true that the term ‘european dimension’ has a different meaning. on the one hand, it refers to the concept of europe, its civilisation, democratic values and projects. however, it can also be seen as european citizenship or european identity, with rights and duties as citizens, active participation and a sense of belonging to europe. it is thus important to have clear views on how to integrate the european dimension in school curricula and how to provide schools with both the material and the opportunities to learn about europe in practice. the commission has already started this work. among our programmes, comenius, for example, supports projects with partners from different countries working on developing the european dimension. the ‘european schoolnet’ is a good example of an interactive and virtual tool for networking and for dissemination. the youth programme also aims to familiarise young people with the concept of a european dimension in their lives through exchanges and especially through voluntary service. transnational projects like these are an excellent example of the european dimension in practice. the recommendation on key competences for lifelong learning, which we have just discussed, is an important step forward. it highlights a number of skills and attitudes needed for active european citizenship as part of social, civic and cultural competences. similarly, our work with national experts on teacher training stresses the importance of european knowledge, mobility and networking. these are a very important part of teachers’ professional development. i fully agree with mr beazley. the commission shares the view that much more needs to be done to raise awareness of the many good national and european initiatives. the commission continues to work with member states, for example co-financing projects within comenius and supporting multilingualism, and we will encourage member states to develop the european dimension as part of their lifelong learning strategies. moreover, my colleague mrs wallström and i recently agreed on a number of initiatives to be taken in this area. therefore, for all these reasons, i see this report
