member of the commission. thank you, mr president, for a stimulating debate. i would like to respond to a couple of the most important issues that have been raised. mr ehler called for better economic analysis of the impact of changes on jobs and growth – and rightly so. on assessing the economic impact of reforms: as i mentioned, the fact there are no plans to harmonise professional regulation across the eu means it would be very difficult to predict impact accurately. we favour comparative assessment of what differences real changes have actually made on the ground in the member states that have already introduced them. that is why we see a strong role for the national authorities, which are well placed when they undertake these analyses, but we will also further reflect on what more we might do to facilitate the building of the economic evidence base at eu level. talking about liberal professions, such as lawyer, requires tough ethical rules and qualities. the commission fully accepts that genuine ethical rules are essential to ensure good governance and practice in professions such as lawyer. in this respect, one standard should apply no matter to whom the services are provided: fixing prices or banning advertising do not deliver high ethical standards and good quality services. quality and observance of ethical standards are better ensured and controlled by adequate training requirements and by effective supervision by the states and/or by professional bodies, including effective complaints procedures for clients. codes of conduct, as mentioned here, also represent a positive step. the commission supports the removal of fixed and minimum prices and the use of result-based fees. there is no evidence to suggest that in the member states where fixed and minimum prices have been removed there has been a deterioration in the quality or ethical standards of legal services. though quality has a price, a fixed price does not in itself guarantee quality. price competition with the possibility of undercutting fixed minimum fees and the use of success fees will, rather, enhance access to justice.
the rapporteur. - mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, let me first of all inform you that commissioner mandelson has contacted me to explain the reasons for his absence from this debate, which i thank him for. the summit on india in finland is the reason; that has given me the opportunity to have an interesting conversation with the commissioner about the agreement with mercosur, showing him that, in addition to india or china, brazil and the whole of mercosur are also emerging powers, a view which the commissioner certainly, and fortunately, also shares. we hope that, once the gloomy outlook of the doha round has been cleared, the electoral process in brazil has been overcome and the political, economic and commercial foundations for relations between the european union and mercosur have been laid, which is what parliament is seeking to do with this report we are presenting today, that the final steps will be taken to bring the negotiations of an ambitious eu-mercosur association agreement to the final stage. we want our report to be that: the relaunch of a political, economic and commercial priority, the establishment of a set of principles, rules and guidelines that bring together a strategic political priority, and the consolidation of the framework of relations between two trading blocs; if we are able to bring them together through an association agreement which, together with the political aspects of cooperation, entails an agreement to create a free trade area, we will have taken the historic step of creating the largest free trade area on the planet. in the present times, when new powers are emerging in the east, this would mean strengthening the mutual interests of two blocs bound together by history and culture, with the benefits that this should bring to our citizens on both continents. we are talking about a population of over 700 million people in all. our report therefore calls for a comprehensive, ambitious and balanced agreement based on three pillars: a political-institutional chapter that strengthens democratic dialogue and political consultation; a cooperation chapter that promotes sustainable economic and social development; and a trade chapter that establishes an advanced free trade area and covers a broad agenda that, in addition to reciprocal liberalisation of trade in goods and services, includes investment, public procurement, protection of intellectual property rights and competition cooperation, as well as trade defence instruments, trade facilitation and a binding dispute settlement mechanism. the examples of mexico and chile are good proof of how our relations can be intensified through an instrument of partnership. the great potential for growth in both directions is evident if we remember that mercosur represents 45% of the population of latin america and represents its most important market, with 45% of gdp. in addition, compared with the rest of latin america, where imports from the united states are three times as high as those from the european union, the eu's share in mercosur is around 25%, compared with 20% for the united states. according to the paris institute of policy studies, the cost of no deal is estimated at some €3.7 billion a year in trade and goods, and more than €5 billion if investment and services are included. the trade agreement must be broad and cover all sectors, although it is logical to recognise the specific sensitivity of certain products, as the report states. we did not want to go over the impact of the agreement in the various subsectors in detail, but we thought it appropriate to analyse the overall, the set of mutual interests of the negotiation. our report therefore addresses both the interests of the eu in mercosur and those of mercosur in the european union and devotes specific sections to such relevant issues as agriculture, with references to subsidies, geographical indications, bioethanol, etc.; nama, where we include a special reference to fisheries and the sensitivity of certain processed products such as canned tuna; services, where real improvements and clear and stable regulatory frameworks are needed; investments, which are fundamental to sustainable economic development and the creation of jobs and wealth; public procurement and intellectual property, as well as the clear identification of possible obstacles to trade and the approximation of certification, accreditation, standardisation, etc. standards, which favour fair trade and fair competition, and the establishment of an agreed dispute settlement mechanism. in addition to the strictly technical and commercial aspects, the report also covers the necessary industrial, labour and social cooperation mechanisms for small and mediumsized enterprises and aspects relating to technology, science, environmental measures, energy and communication, as well as aid and solidarity mechanisms from the european union. finally, we mention the interparliamentary cooperation between the european parliament and the mercosur parliament which is necessary to give the agreement greater democratic representativeness and to bring the sometimes excessively technical aspects of the agreement closer to the feelings of the citizens whom we represent, thus giving the agreement a greater popular dimension. we believe that this report makes clear the european parliament's commitment to a broad and ambitious association agreement between the old and a large part of the new continent, which we want to integrate, and we ask the commission to speed up the negotiations so that the agreement becomes a reality as soon as possible, for the sake of the citizens of both continents. i would like to conclude, mr president, by thanking all the groups in this parliament for their invaluable understanding and support, which has been very much appreciated and which i wanted to be as wide as possible, in the interests of a desirable and broad consensus.

ladies and gentlemen, i would now like to make a statement, and i shall do so standing up, on the so-called 'hungarian revolution' of october 1956. it is half a century since the hungarian people rose up against the communist dictatorship and against the occupation by a foreign power. on october 23, 1956, hungarian university students marched through the streets of budapest in protest against the communist government, and they were quickly joined by citizens of all professions and social conditions. i have to tell you, this is my first childhood memory of politics. at that time, the resistance of the hungarian people invaded the news in my country. i remember the teacher at school explaining to us on a map the place of the events, the voices on the radio stations and the photographs in the newspapers of the t-34 tanks burned in the center of budapest. it was for me the awakening to the notion of freedom struggle. for two weeks there was hope; then the radios went silent and an iron silence was imposed, behind which were thousands of dead and hundreds of exiles. for a time, the budapest uprising hoped that the free west would come to their aid; it did not. for a time, they were led to believe that it would be. we were helpless spectators as thousands of hungarian men, women and children fled their country and sought refuge in the west. this was an indescribable tragedy for the hungarian people, but it was also the first crack that appeared in the soviet system - a crack that would later grow and eventually bring down the berlin wall - and, without a doubt, a great moment in the history of that country. at that time, at the end of june, also in poland the poznan uprising, with the workers of the cegielski factory demanding bread and freedom, was another important moment of that revolt. those events were, no doubt, related. in fact, during the celebration ceremony organized this year to commemorate the events in poznan in 1956, the hungarian president, laszlo sólyom, said that poznan and hungary stood together against the soviet occupation. on 24 october 1956 the hungarians took to the streets with banners on which they had written "poznan-warsaw-budapest". that was the inspiration for what happened next, although it took time. it took time, until spring blossomed in prague in 1968. it took time, until the strikes in poland in 1970, which led to the recognition of solidarnosc, ten years later, as the picket line that brought down the wall. the story came back in 1989. hungary and poland laid the foundation stone for the reunification of the continent, and i think this is a good moment to quote the speech made by albert camus in 1957 on the first anniversary of the hungarian revolution. camus said: "victorious, chained hungary has done more for freedom and justice than any other european nation in the last twenty years . . . in the present loneliness of europe we have only one means of remaining loyal to hungary: never to betray, either in ourselves or in others, that for which the hungarian fighters died, and never to justify, even indirectly, what killed them. it won't be easy to prove ourselves worthy of such a sacrifice. but we must try to do so in a europe that is finally united, forgetting our grievances, making amends for our mistakes, multiplying our efforts and our solidarity. today, a united europe is ready to make further progress and to spread the european spirit even further, contributing to the building of a world in which freedom, solidarity and progress are the guiding principles of our action. that's what we owe to those who died for believing in a free europe. opinion of the committee on fisheries mr president, our committee has made some comments on the cuts introduced by the council in relation to the european commission's proposals. the most important of these cuts is €10 million from the reserve on international agreements, which 'disappears' for both commitments and payments. the committee on fisheries understands that this could even create problems in relation to the union's legal obligations in this area and we therefore ask that the initial amounts be restored. the other reductions made by the council concern european fisheries fund payments: eur 23 million for convergence regions and eur 7 million for those not included in this category. the committee on fisheries believes that if these cuts were to be made, the advance payment of 7% as provided for in the fund's own regulation would be impossible. the overall allocation for fisheries is modest enough, ladies and gentlemen, that these cuts seem unacceptable to us. in addition to being arbitrary and unjustified, they send a very negative signal at a critical moment for the sector, which is why the committee on fisheries calls for the figures proposed by the commission in the preliminary draft budget to be reinstated.

president of the republic of hungary. mr president, members of the european parliament, representatives of the council and the commission, ladies and gentlemen, hungary and the world celebrate together the 50th anniversary of the 1956 hungarian revolution and the fight for freedom. it is encouraging and elevating to feel that there is one commemorative event with which everyone can identify. there are no differences of opinion, no reservations. everyone pays tribute to the memory of the hungarian heroes of 1956. now, after 50 years, with a historical perspective, and after the fall of the soviet communist regime, we can clearly see the historic importance of the 1956 hungarian revolution and the fight for freedom. but this is also an event when the world celebrates itself – and it has every reason to do so. we can re-experience together the former enthusiasm with which peoples took sides with the hungarian revolution. the world can now celebrate its generous sacrifice: austria, which had just been liberated, opening the borders for 160 000 hungarian refugees; the blood donations in poland to help to rescue those wounded in the fight for freedom; the tens of thousands of hungarian refugees who found new homes in various countries around the world. but the real reason for this commemoration and joy is that hungary today is an independent, sovereign and democratic state, with the rule of law, where the country can become a member of international organisations, such as the european union, of its own free will. it is to the credit of 1956 that the world looks upon hungary with a positive mind. the heroic struggle of the hungarian freedom-fighters against soviet predominance has earned hungary recognition and appreciation everywhere up to the present day. it has become the custom, since the collapse of the soviet union, to present the hungarian revolution as a mortal blow to the soviet world system. that is not how anyone saw it during the early years of the military compulsion and the years of terror dispensed by the kádár system. at most, 1956 questioned the communist ideology and presented a dilemma to the left-wing, pro-soviet section of the intelligentsia in western europe, by making them face facts. these attitudes can still be seen as a measure of intellectual sincerity. but politically, the soviet union had learnt that it could assert itself in the region without hindrance or constraint: the western powers had no direct security or economic interests there. there was an ambivalence between the real political intentions and propaganda of the great powers, and thereby an ambivalence in the expectations of the hungarian nation. neither the american nor the french or british governments intended to intervene, or even query the integrity of the soviet sphere of influence – they made this clear to the soviet union in october. but they left the hungarian government isolated and uninformed and the freedom-fighters and the population under a misapprehension, for the propaganda of the state-sponsored western radio stations urged them to trust in the arrival of liberating assistance. the communists could build the berlin wall in 1961 and use military intervention to crush the prague spring reform movement in 1968. what caused it to relinquish its sphere of influence in the baltic and central and eastern europe in 1989, and the collapse itself, was not 1956, but inherent systemic weaknesses and the soviet union’s inability to compete either economically or in the arms race. from another point of view, however, the hungarian revolution and struggle for independence provided the first and weightiest evidence of the instability of the communist regimes in the central european states, which possessed different historical, political, and cultural traditions from those of the soviet union. these states had traditions of democracy. national independence had become something of almost intrinsic value. the struggles in poland and hungary in 1956, in czechoslovakia in 1968, and in poland again, headed by the solidarity trade union, from the 1980s onwards, were concurrently struggles for basic democratic freedoms and for limiting soviet influence. these events and struggles led to the democratic transitions in central europe in 1989-90. a common feature of the 1956 revolution and the change of regime in 1989 is that both rejected party-state communism. faithfulness to the revolution and the legitimacy of our claims to it depend on whether we allow the line between our free hungary today and the hungary we had before 1989 to blur. the parallel lesson of 1956 and 1989 is that in both cases, history surpassed the aspirations that wanted more freedom within a socialist system. the greatness of premier imre nagy lies in the fact that he recognised that. he stepped out of his communist past; he stepped out of the soviet world system. he remained a left-wing politician, but he undertook an historic role, he accepted the fate that the revolutionary hungarian nation offered to him. and he would rather die than retreat. am 22. oktober, dem vorabend der revolution, nahmen staatsoberhäupter, ministerpräsidenten und andere hohe gäste an der festveranstaltung in der budapester staatsoper teil. eingeladen waren unter anderem die staaten, die in jenen tagen viele ungarische flüchtlinge aufgenommen hatten. bis ende 1956 flüchteten mehr als 153 000 ungarn nach österreich. später kamen weitere 30 000 personen dazu. österreich sorgte selbstlos für die unterbringung und verpflegung der flüchtlinge und organisierte die fast unentbehrlich gewordene internationale hilfe. die unterstützung erstreckte sich auf beratung, rechtshilfe, arbeitsvermittlung und sogar auf die unterrichtung der schulkinder und die seelsorge. österreich bereitete auch den weg für die auswanderung in drittländer. ein zehntel der ungarn blieb jedoch in österreich, einem land, dem sich die ungarn immer nahe fühlten. die hilfe österreichs erschöpfte sich jedoch nicht in der flüchtlingshilfe. dieses nachbarland verfolgte die ereignisse nicht nur aus geographischer nähe, sondern brachte ungarn eine besondere empathie entgegen. die besatzungstruppen hatten erst vor kurzem das land verlassen, die rote armee war erst vor kurzem aus wien abgezogen. in österreich wusste man, was das leben in einem nicht freien land bedeutete. hier erfuhr man auch tag für tag, wie der mangel an selbstbestimmung alles durchdringt und schadet. wir teilten auch die erfahrung der totalitären systeme. wir schulden auch der bundesrepublik deutschland besonderen dank. am 2. november 1956 kamen die ersten ungarischen flüchtlinge nach deutschland. als die regierung die große zahl der flüchtlinge erkannte, entschied sie sich, 10 % der flüchtlinge asyl zu gewähren, obwohl sie am 7. november zuerst nur 3 000 flüchtlinge aufnehmen wollte. obwohl die flüchtlinge und vertriebenen aus den östlichen bundesländern bereits eine schwere last für das deutsche versorgungssystem bedeuteten, empfing man die ungarn mit großer sympathie. das deutsche rote kreuz gab insgesamt 30 millionen dm für die unterstützung der flüchtlinge aus. 20 000 ungarische flüchtlinge fanden ein neues zuhause in deutschland. 1 200 studenten konnten in das deutsche hochschulwesen eingegliedert werden und in kastl errichtete man ein zweisprachiges gymnasium. dafür danke ich im namen des ungarischen volkes. ötvenhat megünneplésének az akkori felszabadulást, annak elemi és tiszta örömét kell megörökítenie. ez sugárzik minden fennmaradt fényképről, minden filmfelvételről, amelyen az 1956. október 23-i tüntetők arca látható. és minden emlékező erről beszél. egy híres írónak az erről szóló szavaival szeretném befejezni. ottlik géza írta: „aki nem volt ott végig, semmiféle költői képzelőerővel, forradalomért lüktető szívvel, akár lángelmével sem tudhatja felfogni, mi volt ez. én sem tudtam volna előre elképzelni, hogy milyen ez a boldogság, amivel az ember járt budapest utcáin – mert nem ismertem, egyszerűen fogalmam sem volt róla, hogy van ilyen boldogság. […] a rongy, a talán túlságosan ronggyá vált élete – senkinek sem drágább, mint a haza absztrakt becsülete. lássa meg az arcokat, vegye észre rajtuk […] a megkönnyebbült nyugalmat! mert ez a döntő: nem bátor elszántság, nem hősies vakmerőség, hanem ez van a szemükben: boldog megkönnyebbülés. mennek együtt vagy külön, mély, boldog nyugalommal neki a tankoknak, a rájuk célzott ágyúknak, gépfegyvereknek. semmi nem drágább nekik, mint a visszanyert emberi méltóságuk.” köszönöm.

president of the council. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, on behalf of the council, i should like to thank mr de keyser for his important and very comprehensive report on the situation in syria. the council agrees with many of the concerns expressed in the report in relation to syria. as de keyser states in his report, syria can play an important role in the middle east as 'a link between the parties to the peace process and as a facilitator of the resolution of regional conflicts'. the council therefore decided in august to authorise the high representative, mr javier solana, and the presidency to liaise with all relevant parties which could have an impact on the solution to the crisis in lebanon and the wider middle east situation. these parties include, of course, syria. after the dramatic events of the summer, it is important to stabilise the situation in lebanon and its neighbouring areas. foreign minister the judge's meeting with the syrian foreign minister at the end of august was a clear message to syria. syria is expected to contribute to the implementation of resolutions 1559, 1680 and 1701. syria must support the national reconstruction process in lebanon and make every effort to stabilise the internal political situation in lebanon. the issue of the supply of arms to non-lebanese forces and the question of arms smuggling will have a major impact on whether a ceasefire can be built on a lasting basis. the demarcation of the lebanese-syrian border and the establishment of diplomatic relations are also open issues. the resolution of the problem area of sheba will also require cooperation with syria. the syrian authorities must also continue to cooperate with the brammertz commission investigating the assassination of former lebanese prime minister hariri. the activities of palestinian organisations based in damascus and the support given to them by syria are an issue outside the scope of resolution 1701 but of importance for stability in the region. the situation in the middle east is also directly affected by the relationship between syria and its actions towards iraq and iran. the council also closely monitored developments in the human rights situation in syria. the arrests of human rights defenders and signatories of the beirut-damascus declaration in spring were particularly worrying. the fact that some of them have been recently released is, of course, welcome. the eu will continue to closely monitor the implementation of the freedoms of expression and assembly in the country. it is clear that syria must also act in accordance with international human rights principles. the reopening of the eu-supported civil society training centre is an important objective. the center closed in the spring, just a week after it opened. continuous contacts with syria shall be maintained in particular through euro-med cooperation. the foreign ministers' meeting in tampere in november, to which syria has also been invited, provides a good forum for discussion. syria is a major player in the middle east. depending on its choice, it can be either a distraction or a constructive partner. syria's historically strong relations with lebanon mean that it has a particularly important role in the implementation of un security council resolutions on the situation in lebanon. the union has consistently stressed the need to respect the right to self-determination and the territorial integrity and political independence of lebanon. it is important for the stability of lebanon and the region as a whole that, among other things, the smuggling of arms into lebanon be prevented. syria must guard its borders to achieve this goal. the council has stated its willingness to improve relations with syria, whose behaviour is in its favour. the ball is now in syria. in the right circumstances, the union may, inter alia, reconsider the possibility of signing an association agreement. this would naturally contribute to cooperation between the eu and syria, particularly in the economic field, and to the reforms necessary for the development of syria, as the report suggests.
, member of the commission. mr president, first of all i think this is a very timely discussion. thank you for putting it on the agenda. i have followed closely the discussions in the afet committee on ms de keyser’s substantive and comprehensive report. the report is a fair account of the internal and regional challenges facing syria. i welcome this reflection by the european parliament on the way forward with syria. after the conflict in lebanon and in the new context of united nations security council resolution 1701 (2006), it is indeed the right moment to reassess where we are with our current policy. syria is a long-standing partner under the barcelona process and is a potential candidate for the european neighbourhood policy in the medium term. i share your view that we have a strong interest in bringing that country closer to europe. syria, as we all know, is an essential player for stability in the middle east. it is a key part of the puzzle when it comes to finding a long-term solution to the conflicts in the region and also in the implementation of resolution 1701 in full. in this critical moment for the peace process, damascus has the power to be part of the solution and not part of the problem. this means that we expect syria, as you have stated in the motion for a resolution, to pass the right messages to hezbollah and hamas, to prevent arms shipments into lebanon, as our colleague from the council has said, and to help with the settlement on the shebaa farms. as i have indicated, i believe that re-engaging with syria should be part of our strategy. a different issue is then whether and how far we can re-engage here and now. the first thing we need in order to re-engage with syria is for its leaders to show their commitment and their interest in moving forward and taking positive steps on a number of issues. as you well know, lately we have gone through difficult times in our relationship with syria. ms de keyser’s report addresses a number of the political divergences. overcoming the political deadlock depends on the leadership’s ability to translate some of its words of goodwill into deeds of goodwill. syria has a new opportunity at this critical time for the peace process to demonstrate that it is serious about contributing positively to regional stability. in the absence of an association agreement, we have limited scope to tackle matters of concern. nevertheless, we have tried where we can, and where we feel it is of interest for the people of syria. we have tried to continue programmes in those areas that directly benefit the citizens of syria. for example, on human rights, the european union uses diplomatic channels to address the most serious violations, including, for instance, the cases of prisoners of conscience. we have also reacted to the limitations on freedom of expression and the wave of arrests that accompanied the publication of the beirut-damascus declaration last may. but it is not by cutting off contacts that we will achieve much progress. with no dialogue, we have no influence. we should therefore turn the situation around, give a positive perspective to relations with syria and set out the areas where we expect progress. we do so in part through our cooperation programmes. syria now seems to be well engaged on the road to economic transition and we welcome the approval of syria’s national agenda for reforms sponsored by deputy prime minister dardari last may. support for the implementation of the reform process, including progressive steps to political opening, could be the focus of our action in the next few years, if things go well. cooperation under the enpi – the european neighbourhood policy instrument – will allow us to give syria the medium-term prospect of full participation in the neighbourhood policy. the enp will then bring additional benefits and, we hope, a more interesting package for them, when the time is ripe. as for the association agreement, it is still on the table. we have finalised all technical preparations and we have initialled the agreement. now, it is pending a decision on signature from the council. signature is a process. so far, political circumstances have not been right. member states still expect syria to take more positive and credible steps to make signature possible, including on regional issues such as lebanon and palestine. syria’s recent statements to facilitate the implementation of security council resolution 1701 may be encouraging signs in this respect, as are president assad’s calls for resuming peace talks, which have had some positive echoes in israel. like the european parliament, the commission is a strong believer in dialogue. therefore, i very much hope that the positive messages that we have received from damascus lately will be transformed into deeds and that we will be able to restore a strong relationship with that country.
i would like to congratulate mrs de keyser on her draft recommendation and on all the work she has been doing on relations with syria. i think it is important that we take this debate into account and place it in the context that is most appropriate to it, mr president. and this context, as the commissioner has very well said, is to take stock of the situation in the transition towards the association agreement, without forgetting that we must also encourage a parliamentary dialogue with syria, given the importance - as has been stressed here - that this country has, from a strategic point of view, in the complex context of the region. but i think it is also important to stress - and the text of the resolution says it very clearly - that we are not at a time when parliament has to give its assent to the association agreement. the resolution 'draft recommendation' says very clearly that the conditions are not yet met: a number of progress must be made in a very clear way. i don't think it's good news that syria has concluded a defense agreement with iran. substantial progress is needed to respect the traditional doctrine of the european union in the field of democracy and respect for human rights. the un security council resolutions must be respected and the territorial integrity of lebanon and syria must be respected. cooperation must be pursued in the investigation of the assassination of former prime minister hariri, and progress must be made in the field of the abolition of the death penalty, respect for religious minorities, etc. i think, therefore, mr president, that there is still a long way to go. there is good news, like the appointment of mr. dandari as deputy prime minister. i had the privilege of meeting him after a mission in lebanon. i believe that it is only on the basis of these premises, as the commissioner said a moment ago, that we must transform this catalogue of good intentions into concrete deeds, so that the european union can give its approval to this important association agreement between the union and syria.
president of the council. mr president, the establishment of the agency and the requirements concerning its tasks, structure and financial management are laid down in the council regulation of 26 october 2004 establishing an agency for the management of operational cooperation at the external borders of the member states of the european union. the regulation provides for the communication to the council of the agency's programme of activities, the general and specific risk analyses prepared by the agency, the annual general report on its activities and the agency's budget. only the commission may propose measures to amend the provisions of the regulation. the adoption of the measures concerning the organisational structure, staff policy and work programme of the agency shall be the primary responsibility of the management board of the agency, in which the council shall not participate. the development of community policy and legislation on external border control remains the responsibility of the eu institutions. close coordination between the agency and the institutions must therefore be ensured and arrangements are in place for this purpose in accordance with the regulation establishing the agency. in this context, i would draw your attention to the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council establishing a mechanism for the establishment of rapid border intervention teams. it is intended to strengthen the operational activities of the agency and to promote solidarity between the member states and the community in crisis situations. the european council last december proposed that the member states, the council and the commission should take a number of measures before the end of this year to improve practical cooperation between member states. these include the strengthening of the control and surveillance of the eu's southern maritime border and the medsea study on the mediterranean coastguard network, which has already been completed by the border agency. in recent months, the council, at its meeting on 24 july and at the informal ministerial meeting in september, has paid particular attention to improving operational cooperation between the member states and the agency, with particular regard to the situation in the mediterranean and africa. the role of the agency and its involvement in operational activities, particularly in the mediterranean and in africa, were discussed. the council welcomed the measures already taken by frontex and the commission and stressed the need to further develop operational cooperation. the council also adopted conclusions on the strengthening of the external maritime border in the south at the beginning of october. in its conclusions, it called on frontex to promote a feasibility study on the establishment of a european surveillance system covering, initially, the whole of the community's southern sea border and the mediterranean. the council also asked the border agency to consider the establishment of interlinked regional centres available to frontex for operational matters in different maritime zones or sub-zones. however, the council should not propose to allocate appropriations to the budget of the agency for additional measures. in accordance with article 33 of the council regulation establishing an agency for the operational management of the external borders of the member states of the european union and the hague programme, the activities of the agency will be evaluated before the end of next year on the basis of an evaluation report by the commission.

member of the commission. mr president, i should like to express my appreciation for the opportunity to respond to some of the questions raised in this debate and to express my thanks for all the positive contributions. if nairobi is a success, it will mean that we have made the right decisions and the right agreements. the commission recognises the need for the european union to maintain its leading role in not only international but also domestic efforts to fight climate change. i agree that it is important to assist developing countries to adapt to the adverse effects of climate change and to help them in deploying sustainable technologies. a few days ago, the commission proposed the new global energy efficiency and renewable energy fund. the anticipated total initial funding from public and commercial sources is eur 100 million. this new initiative aims to boost climate-friendly technologies in africa in particular. in addition, we have the adaptation fund. we hope it will be agreed in nairobi to make this operational. the fund will be financed by 2% on the proceeds of the clean development mechanism. we expect about eur 350 million to be available for investments in developing countries and in africa for the period 2008 to 2012. the european union can only be credible in its leadership role when it achieves meaningful reductions in domestic emissions and complies with international commitments under the kyoto protocol. the second national allocation plans of the european union emissions trading scheme will be a decisive test. if member states put more allowances into the european market than companies are likely to emit collectively, the european union emissions trading scheme would fail. mr davies said that collectively the first 17 plans notified propose a total allocation that exceeds 2005 emissions of these member states by about 15%, which is really a lot. i am determined that we shall not permit the european union emissions trading scheme to fail and the commission will assess all the national allocation plans in a consistent and fair manner. all the member states will have to contribute to the success of the emissions trading scheme in the period 2008 to 2012. i agree that we should try very hard with our public relations and the possibilities for influencing our governments, but also your involvement and action is important in this crucial phase of the emissions trading scheme. i would ask you that together we ensure that, in all the capitals of the member states and in brussels, this debate on the allocation is about how much more we should reduce, rather than how much more we can emit. in the next few days, a communication on the emissions trading scheme should be adopted by the commission, launching a review of this important scheme. this will address its scope, how to make it simpler and more predictable, strengthening compliance and linking up with emissions trading schemes elsewhere. as regards tackling transport emissions, which contribute to about 22% of the emissions in the european union, this year the commission will put forward a legislative proposal to include the aviation sector in european union emissions trading. also this year, the commission will review the possibilities for further reductions of carbon dioxide emissions from cars after 2008-2009, with a view to meeting the community target of 120g of carbon dioxide per kilometre by 2012. that will, of course, require legislation. the commission is also exploring options for a legal framework in the european union to allow the safe capture and underground storage of carbon dioxide from industrial installations, provided that that is considered appropriate. the commission also intends to promote adaptation measures, helping the regional and national decision-makers to deal with increasingly evident impacts of climate change. on the basis of a green paper on adaptation to climate change, to be launched at a conference in brussels on 1 december, the commission will begin a public debate on the need to adapt to unavoidable climate change. most importantly, we will have to further frame the international debate after 2012. next january, the commission is planning to release its energy package. a core part of the package will be the strategic european union energy review. this will put forward an alternative energy scenario for the european union that is in line with the european union’s long-term climate change objective. close to the adaptation of the energy package, the commission will also be releasing a green paper on the european union’s views on further action to tackle climate change. this green paper will respond to the european council’s request to develop a european union strategy to limit global warming to 2°c, compared to pre-industrial levels. it will identify concrete proposals, both within the european union and internationally, for achieving that objective. one of our main objectives will be to bring on board the united states and other fast-developing countries like china and india in a common but differentiated way, as provided for by the united nations convention on climate change. the commission will ensure that the energy package and the green paper put forward a climate and energy strategy for the european union that is coherent, coordinated and sustainable. i the commission's vice-president mr president, ladies and gentlemen, members of the house. i would first like to congratulate mrs wortmann-kool on this excellent report. the resolution shows that there is a broad agreement between parliament, the council and the commission on the promotion of inland waterway transport. water transport is safe, low-polluting, energy-efficient and offers large spare capacities. despite its advantages, inland waterway transport is underused: it accounts for only 6% of the total land transport of goods in the union, while in some member states its modal share is 40%. today, europe has 36,000 km of navigable waterways. it is a true transeuropean network. we need a european vision to promote this mode of transport. it can achieve a much larger modal share if, as you have just pointed out, madam president, our vision is accompanied by concrete actions. i thank parliament for its support for me in this report by mrs wortmann-kool. i shall confine myself, mr president, to a few comments on the main points, starting with the improvement of market conditions. we must develop new, innovative and multimodal services to enable inland navigation to play its role between the major seaports and the major cities in the hinterland. the inland waterway sector is characterised by more than 70% small businesses, often boat builders. the conditions for strengthening their market position must be created, for example by improving access to finance by removing regulatory and administrative barriers and by providing clear indications of state aid. the commission will start work on state aid to this sector. these guidelines are expected to be published in 2008-09. that's for market conditions. as regards fleet modernisation, inland navigation needs to improve its logistical efficiency and environmental and safety performance. innovations must be in the area of shipbuilding - for example, engines and propulsion - and in information and communication technologies for what are known as river information services. a regulatory framework already exists but real implementation of the system needs to be ensured. this also applies to the standards for fuels for inland waterway transport. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the quality of the products is not compromised. i come now to the promotion of employment and skills. the shipping industry is suffering from a shortage of crews and a growing shortage of candidates for succession to the companies. the strategy should focus on improving working and living conditions on board and vocational training. i intend to propose harmonisation of crew and licence requirements through mutual recognition in 2008. the image of river navigation must be corrected, as it is currently the image of inland navigation. the real potential of inland waterway transport must be made known by setting up a network to promote transport by waterways, as is the case in some regions. as regards river infrastructure, there are bottlenecks within the network which hinder the competitiveness of waterway transport. the obstacles must therefore be removed. this is primarily the responsibility of the member states, but the community can contribute to this through the transeuropean networks. in this context, the commission gives priority to the development of the two main river routes: the rhine-meuse-danube route and the seine-escaut link. in the new financial regulation submitted to parliament for approval, we have proposed a 30% rate of support for river projects and the inclusion of these projects in the multiannual programme. i hope that the council, like parliament, will follow our proposals. the contribution of intelligent transport systems is indispensable. we are preparing the implementation of river information services. it is in fact a system for managing information on inland waterway transport, which will enable boatmen to plan their journeys better, reduce waiting times at locks and ensure continuous monitoring of transport. madam rapporteur, you mentioned the appointment of a ten coordinator. i must say that we have been able to appreciate the positive results achieved by the six coordinators already in place. president costa has also asked for the appointment of a coordinator for inland waterway transport, as well as for maritime transport. i'm telling you, my intention is to pick two coordinators in the next few weeks. the naiades programme provides for a wide range of actions: regulatory harmonization, strategic promotion and coordination measures. however, all these actions will only be effective if the institutional framework is appropriate. today, however, we are faced with a fragmentation of resources and a dispersion of efforts at different levels. the framework must therefore be adapted to the requirements of the enlarged european market. we're looking at a number of options. the results of this analysis will be discussed with all the parties concerned, with the member states and the international river commissions. in conclusion, this naiades programme must be a success and to this end, it must be possible to count on the support of those responsible at all levels: national, regional authorities, river boards and companies. i thank parliament and you, mrs wortmann-kool, for sending a strong signal with this report in favour of the promotion of inland waterway transport, which europe needs more than ever.

interest rates, inflation was two tenths of 2%, and there was a modest growth in the euro area of 1.4%. these are the macroeconomic data, but the results of monetary policy require to complement this the rapporteur. mr president, this is the first time that this parliament has discussed a report on the economic situation in the euro area and that is why i attach particular importance to this report, especially as this debate, this analysis, which we are carrying out jointly for the first time, is taking place at a time when the situation is politically complex and economically doubtful. i say politically complex, because, in dealing here with institutional questions, i cannot ignore the ongoing debate on what to do with the constitutional treaty. i cannot ignore the fact that this report is being discussed in a 'new era' of monetary policy, with interest rates that have been rising for some time and threaten to continue rising, at a time when we are launching the stability and growth pact as revised by the commission and when, for the first time, member states are coming before the european institutions to give an account of what they have done with the lisbon strategy in their national reform plans. i say confused economic situation because, while it is true - and i share the commission's analysis - that the economic situation is good, much better than it was in previous stages, i want to stress that our potential growth, 2%, is not enough to absorb european unemployment, to keep up with our competitors and to maintain our standard of living. the report is structured, as is traditional in this house, around several headings: macroeconomic policies, reforms, with particular emphasis on the internal market, and institutional questions, with emphasis on the coordination of economic policies and external representation. in the field of macroeconomic policy, there is no great change from what we said in the debate on the broad economic guidelines. the recipe in macroeconomic policies is more stability, more stability, and more stability. in relation to monetary policy, what we emphasize - and i repeat, institutional issues - is that we would like more transparency and clarity in the european central bank. we'd like to know why he does what he does and how he manages and doses the two pillars on which he bases his decisions. we therefore ask for the publication of the short minutes setting out the arguments for and against a particular decision. as regards budgetary policy, the first finding of this report is that the momentum of monetary policy may be losing its momentum and the torch must be passed to budgetary policy, which leads us, as i have stressed before, to ask the commission to interpret the stability and growth pact strictly and to ask the member states to make a greater effort to reduce their deficits, especially in times of 'fat cow disease'. we also call for a new approach, namely greater coordination of the budgetary timetables and of the forecasts which the member states take into account when setting their budgetary scenarios. it is not necessary for countries participating in the european economic union to have different forecasts on oil prices, interest rates or exchange rates; we would like to know what we are talking about in the discussions we have with the national parliaments. as regards public debt, we also call for a stronger effort to reduce public debt, as is traditional, to free up resources and to address the lisbon strategy and the budgetary challenges that will arise from the ageing of the population. the last point - which has been repeated - is a review of tax systems to promote the competitiveness of the european economy. in the field of reforms, the recipe is lisbon and more lisbon. we want the public to know what the behaviour of each member state is. we therefore call for a code of conduct which will allow us to put more pressure on the most backward and which will also allow them, through the export of good practice, to know how the smartest people in the class work. in the internal market: freedom, more freedom against the protectionist temptations of recent times; development of the services market. in short, consolidation of the fundamental freedoms. on institutional matters - i want to focus on the better functioning of the union - we are asking for a trialogue - i know the commissioner is not enthusiastic about the idea - between the council, the commission and parliament, to be held quarterly, in parallel with the dialogue we have with the european central bank. we ask, in order to facilitate this dialogue, that the eurogroup draw up a road map indicating where the euro area is heading in the next two years. we ask the commission to provide us with a more precise set of tools for encouraging dialogue in subsequent reports and we invite the commissioner and the council to meet with us every quarter. the commission's external representation is not consistent with the international weight of the euro. we welcome the fact that the member states have acted with one voice in singapore, at the meetings of the international institutions, and we call for more coordination and imaginative efforts to have a single representation of the member states in the international monetary fund, the world bank and the other international institutions. i thank all the alternative rapporteurs and all the colleagues for the effort they have made.

president of the court of auditors. madam president, mr kallas, ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen, i would like to thank you for your work. i am delighted to be able to take part in your debate today in the european parliament's plenary on the court's 29th annual report for the financial year 2005. i have already presented this report to the committee on budgetary control in strasbourg on 23 october and to the economic and financial affairs council in brussels on 7 november. each court's annual report is the culmination of complex and in-depth on-the-spot audits carried out by its auditors at all levels involved in the management of eu funds over the previous 12 months. in accordance with the principles of international auditing standards and as confirmed by external experts, the court's audit evidence is based on the in-depth examination of sample transactions from each budgetary area and on assessments of the functioning of internal control systems for expenditure. only serious formal errors and errors with financial implications, overstatements of expenditure, ineligible beneficiaries and ineligible expenditure shall form the basis for the court's statement of assurance. the court has a strong interest in, and a treaty obligation since its inception, conducting cost-effectiveness studies, the results of which are published in its special reports. in addition, the court's assessments of internal control systems, which are required for the annual declaration of assurance, provide an important basis for these economic assessments. allow me to turn now to the court's main findings of 2005. as regards the areas where significant improvements can be made, the court duly acknowledges that the commission has successfully implemented the changeover from cash to accrual accounting. the court concludes that the consolidated accounts for 2005 are reliable for the eu's general budget, which totals eur 105 billion. however, i have to limit this confirmatory note because the assets were overvalued net and the demarcation procedures were not applied consistently. the court may re-affirm its unconditional approval of the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions in respect of the eu's revenue, commitments, administrative expenditure and pre-accession strategy, with the exception of sapard. the integrated administration and control system (iacs) which covers 56% of expenditure under the common agricultural policy is also a positive development. as in 2004, the court confirms that invekos, when applied correctly, is successful in preventing irregular agricultural expenditure. in practice, this is the case for the eu-15 with the exception of greece, and although the implementation of invekos is progressing well in the new eu member states, these systems are not yet fully effective. as the court's detailed audit evidence shows, the other areas of expenditure, which represent the bulk of the eu budget in value terms, continue to be marked by material errors as regards the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions. in other words, the court cannot again issue a full endorsement, in particular for the agricultural expenditure as a whole, structural measures, internal policies and external policies. this is due to the numerous irregularities detected, such as overdeclarations of expenditure, double counting of costs, ineligible beneficiaries and/or ineligible projects, non-realised expenditure and non-compliance with the objectives of the public procurement rules. these irregularities are due to the inadequacy of the current internal controls on eu expenditure. the ec treaty requires the commission to ensure that internal control systems are in place and function effectively in practice at all levels of the eu administration. the court has not only found evidence of poor controls on payments in the context of shared management in agriculture and structural measures, but also that the commission is not setting a good example in the eu's internal and external policy spending that it directly manages. for example, in the area of research, the commission's checks of declarations of expenditure were significantly reduced in 2005, despite the persisting high error rate and the inherent risk of this type of expenditure. the commission argues that the errors detected and pointed out by the court are of minor importance in that errors and irregularities in the final closure of programmes are detected and corrected in the course of the various corrective mechanisms covering several years. the court's audit work shows that in practice these corrections are insufficient and not targeted at final beneficiaries in all areas. in addition, recovery procedures are not without their shortcomings. for example, in the context of shared management with the member states, the following has been identified: the commission has also been asked to submit a report on the implementation of the budget. the last year of full closure was 1998. in addition, fines imposed by means of conformity decisions for systemic deficiencies are imposed only by the authorities of the member states. since in most cases overpaid amounts are not recovered from the final beneficiaries, the burden falls on the national taxpayers and not on the final beneficiaries who claim excessive costs. as regards structural operations, the accounts for the 1994-99 programmes are still incomplete and, in the court's view, some programmes which have been closed still have a significant error rate. in addition, the commission closed some programmes without financial corrections, despite substantial reservations about the expenditure certified. this is a clear indication of the risk that in practice errors in interim payment applications will not be corrected. i would like to stress that the court of justice naturally welcomes recoveries for the benefit of the eu budget. however, it should be noted that the flat-rate financial corrections are made for weaknesses in the control systems of the member states and therefore do not normally lead to the correction of errors related to the legality and regularity of the underlying transactions at the level of the final beneficiaries. the court considers that these shortcomings should be addressed by: there is a need for a logical chain of effective internal controls based on clear and appropriate rules and common principles and standards, taking into account the risk assessment in terms of the type of operations and forms of management. similarly, effective systems of recovery and sanctions should apply in all areas of the eu budget. the european court of auditors, for its part, is seeking to develop more closely, together with the national audit authorities, areas of common interest. for the contact committee of the presidents of the supreme audit institutions to be held in warsaw next month, the court calls for the existing cooperation to be extended to the evaluation of internal control systems in the member states. the european union is facing new challenges with the operational arrangements, the closure and completion of the current expenditure programmes in the field of the structural funds and the launch of the programmes for the period 2007-13 and the forthcoming accession of two new member states. let me conclude by explaining how eu financial management should address these challenges. the commission, together with the member states' authorities, must ensure that effective and reliable internal control systems exist at all levels of the eu administration, which in turn include sufficient audits, are properly carried out, recorded and monitored, and are based on simplified rules for eu expenditure. the aim of all of us should be a european union which manages its budget efficiently for the benefit of the citizens of the union. thank you for your kind attention.
vice-president of the european commission madam president, mr weber, ladies and gentlemen, i presented my preliminary position on the annual report to the committee on budgetary control on 23 october. the commission is currently actively working on the follow-up and correction of the errors identified. the commission sent a letter to the member states the day after the court's report was published, asking them to comment and explain the errors found in the member state concerned and to correct them. we therefore take full and timely account of the court's findings. but, like you, the commission has reflected on the political implications of the report since it was published. it is clear that this report is not yet a general positive affirmative statement. as president weber said, the court of auditors will make a positive declaration on the 'legality and regularity' of the expenditure, the commitments, the pre-accession strategy, the administrative expenditure and the expenditure of the common agricultural policy which form part of the single administrative and control system. however, the court does not give a positive affirmative opinion on other areas, such as research programmes and the structural funds. the main reason for this is that the court has found too many errors in the selection of transactions in these areas. as president weber said, the errors are caused by 'negligence or error, poor knowledge of complex rules and presumably fraud against the eu budget'. i think that the criticisms made by the court of auditors in the context of last year's audit are unfortunately justified in the area of research programmes. the reduction in the number of follow-up audits in this sensitive area by almost half should have been abandoned, but the recovery procedure should be faster and more robust. it is true that we missed many errors that the court of auditors later discovered. i believe that the mistakes made in this area, as in others, are mainly due to a lack of knowledge of complex rules. in fact, i think the commission has done too little and too slowly to simplify and clarify the rules. we will address these issues in the action plan and in the proposals for the new programming period. we can only welcome the court's continued attention and advice to improve the situation. i'd like to address the fraud next. how much fraud is there in the implementation of the eu budget? each suspected case of fraud is thoroughly investigated by olaf, as evidenced by recent cases reported in the press concerning the chernobyl project and the infrastructure and logistics office. but is the entire eu budget a fraud, as some journalists write year after year? let me quote from a report published yesterday by the house of lords on the management and audit of eu funds. the report says that the press coverage often suggests that corruption is widespread in the european institutions. our investigation found nothing to support this view. the commission has estimates based on data from the member states for the two areas with the highest expenditure: agriculture and regional aid. according to these estimates, 13 to 15% of the reported irregularities, i.e. 0,05% of agricultural expenditure and 0,53% of structural and cohesion fund expenditure, are suspected of fraud. last year, the commission deducted eur 90 million in claims for non-performing loans, which is about 0.09% of the budget. so the fraud rate is negligible. which doesn't mean we shouldn't seriously fight every single case. this appears to be confirmed by the court's audit results for 2005. of all the information, all the audits and some nine hundred transactions in the sample examined by the court in 2005, only four gave rise to suspicions of fraud or serious irregularities that were reported to the anti-fraud office. however, olaf's analysis did not confirm fraud in any of the cases reported. however, the court has again provided useful data which olaf can use in its ongoing work. mr president, madam president, now that comments have been made on our shortcomings, the need for simplification and the level of fraud, i expect the discharge authority to also want to assess the impact of the errors found on the 'quality/price' ratio. the court's report (page 138) shows that the court audited 95 projects financed by the structural funds and found significant errors in 60 of them. does this mean that two thirds of the structural funds have been lost or wasted? does this mean that the objectives of these projects have not been achieved? obviously, it's not. some pioneering research may not have had all the necessary paperwork done, although similarly there may be projects which have been carried out with exemplary due diligence and all the paperwork done, but whose objectives have not been achieved. unfortunately, the report does not provide information on the actual impact of community funding. the question therefore arises: what conclusions can parliament and the citizens of the member states draw from the court's overview of the structural policy failures? the court of auditors is accustomed to claiming that it is only a messenger and that, under the treaty, it must make a declaration of assurance each year on the whole budget. the court does this by sampling transactions and by carrying out other audits. he's checking to see if the rules are being followed. the court shall carry out this work in a professional manner and in accordance with the availability of human resources. but who is to judge how errors affect the achievement of policy objectives? what should be the basis for the european parliament's assessment? you are the budgetary authority, together with the council, which has the final say on the allocation of funds. the court's reports should provide you with a basis for assessing the effectiveness of the implementation of the budgets approved so far. in this context, i think that the court should be called upon to assess the material impact of the errors. we know that the court has the necessary competence. in the special reports, he provides estimates of the 'price-quality ratio', which we find very useful. why not include such an analysis in the annual report? the commission considers sound financial management to be the achievement of policy objectives in an efficient and cost-effective manner. the commission considers that the scheme will be implemented over a period of several years, ensuring that the costs of the control scheme are balanced against the revenue generated by it. the commission is well aware that few university professors applying for funding for research programmes have the skills of an accountant and may therefore make mistakes in their applications. but should research funding be stopped because of this? no, not at all. we'll reduce the margin of error, but we'll deal with the rest. there is probably one option missing between a negative and a positive affirmative. the court of auditors is required by the treaty to assess the soundness of financial management (article 248 (2) of the ec treaty). could it also assess whether the commission has taken the necessary measures to ensure a good price-quality ratio in a given year? this would not make the commission's task any easier, but it would give all of us the right perspective for our actions. perhaps you think it's too radical? perhaps this is too radical, but the report published by the house of lords yesterday is even more radical. the report of the court of auditors states that 'there is a need to improve the methods of submitting the confirmatory declaration' and suggests, inter alia, that the court 'must clearly distinguish between irregularity and fraud by publishing separately the details of fraudulent transactions and administrative errors' and that 'the confirmatory declaration should, in particular, provide a detailed summary of financial management for each category of expenditure and member state' and list 'member states which mismanage european funds'. the commission will study this interesting report carefully. let me also touch on the issue of recall. in this year's confirmatory statement, the court seems to have expressed doubts as to whether the amounts to be recovered should be taken into account in the confirmatory statement. the court of auditors states that the recovery of the amounts does not invalidate the act and does not protect the beneficiaries from committing errors. the commission considers that this view does not accurately reflect the reality. each year, the commission recovers large sums from the member states, which in turn recover them from the beneficiaries. this system shall contribute to the protection of the financial interests of the union. it has a preventive effect by stimulating member states to improve their administrative and control systems and to prevent, detect and recover from beneficiaries irregular payments. we, or rather the member states, should have earned the credit for the recovery. recovery should also be taken into account in the statement of assurance. madam chairman, i'll move on to the more joyous topic. the commission has established working relations with the inspection authorities of several member states. the idea of a joint audit of eu funds has been well received by them. i am very encouraged by the statement by president weber that the court of auditors intends to start joint audits with the national audit authorities, starting with the structural funds and the financial corrections in the member states. in fact, we would be better able to persuade the member states to take more responsibility for spending the eu budget if the court of auditors took account of and used national audit findings in its work. finally, a note on the welcome message contained in the court's report. president weber has indicated that 'the commission has implemented the new accounting system with considerable speed and is now able to obtain from it the necessary additional information which is much more complete than the information provided under the former cash-based system'. we are proud of this achievement. in conclusion, the affirmative is once again negative. the commission regrets that. we will correct the errors made and take measures to address the deficiencies in the system in accordance with the action plan for the establishment of a single internal control framework. the commission acknowledges that there is still a lot of work to be done, but points out that every year there is significant progress and that eu funds are generally managed in a credible manner. the situation is under control, but more needs to be done to simplify complex rules. i and my colleagues look forward to more in-depth sectoral discussions at future budget implementation hearings. finally, the commission would like to stress once again that there is no link between the list of errors contained in the court's report and the discharge procedure. the commission would also welcome the inclusion of performance, i.e. the 'price/quality ratio', in the audit. we believe that this would help the discharge authority in its important task. thank you for your attention!
